marketplace.name: ai-foundry
marketplace.description: The AI Foundry (BYU Marriott) toolbox for building your own Claude Code harness: an 8-stage SDLC framework plus skills, agents and hooks, each labeled proven (runs in production in our harness) or new (written for this marketplace).

stages.name: Scaffold
stages.goal: the project has the full artifact set, so every later stage has a place to write.
stages.artifact: README.md, REQUIREMENTS.md, DECISIONS.md, PRD.md, WORKPLAN.md, CHANGELOG.md, stories.json, stories.schema.json, done-journey.yaml, plus `tools/gen_stories.py`. Templates: `templates/*`.

stages.name: Requirements
stages.goal: know exactly what was asked, by whom, and what already exists.
stages.gate: every ask is verbatim with an R-id and a source. The "Already exists" audit is filled. No `TODO` markers remain.
stages.artifact: `REQUIREMENTS.md` (template `templates/REQUIREMENTS.md`) with each ask verbatim and an R-id (R-01, R-02...) plus its source and date, and `DECISIONS.md` (template `templates/DECISIONS.md`) with human decisions recorded verbatim.

stages.name: PRD + stories
stages.goal: a PRD whose stories can be checked by someone who did not write them.
stages.gate: stories have observable criteria. The `prd-critic` agent's critiques are addressed in Appendix A. `gen_stories.py --check` exits 0. Every R-id is covered by a story or explicitly dropped.
stages.artifact: `PRD.md` (template `templates/PRD.md`) with inline stories in the form `**US-01. Title.**` followed by numbered, observable acceptance criteria, and `stories.json` compiled from it (schema `templates/stories.schema.json`). Never hand-edit a title or a criterion in stories.json; only `status`, `notes` and `evidence` are edited there.

stages.name: Workplan
stages.goal: a plan that agents can execute in parallel and humans can read in one minute.
stages.gate: every task has an owner, model, effort and review tier. Milestones exist. The "Blocked on human" list exists.
stages.artifact: `WORKPLAN.md` (template `templates/WORKPLAN.md`): a task table `Id | Task | Owner | Deps | Status` where Owner names the model, effort and review tier, plus milestone checkboxes (`- [ ] M1.1 title`), "Next up", and "Blocked on human".

stages.name: Execute
stages.goal: build each task in isolation, then merge it back.
stages.gate: every task is DONE or PARKED, with evidence.
stages.artifact: code, one branch per lane (`lane/<task-id>-<slug>`), one worktree per lane (`../<repo>-lanes/<task-id>`), one PR per lane.

stages.name: Code QA
stages.goal: the code does what the tests say, and nothing downstream broke.
stages.gate: each change has a test. The blast radius of shared changes was checked. CI is green.

stages.name: Visual QA with example users
stages.goal: the deployed build works for real kinds of users on the devices they use.
stages.gate: the done gate exits 0 on the deployed build, and every acceptance criterion is PASS. INCONCLUSIVE is not a pass.

stages.name: Ship
stages.goal: users know what they can now do, and the record says what is LIVE and why.
stages.gate: the gate passed, then the changelog, then the users were told what to try. Never in the other order.
stages.artifact: `CHANGELOG.md` (template `templates/CHANGELOG.md`) with a dated entry, and story status `LIVE` with `evidence` in stories.json.

stages.name: Feedback
stages.goal: every bug makes the system stronger, and features graduate on evidence.
stages.gate: each bug has a story and a test that fails before the fix. A human decides when a feature graduates.
stages.artifact: new R-ids and stories (or criteria) in the PRD, and regression tests that fail before the fix.

plugins.name: foundry-sdlc
plugins.description: The 8-stage 0-to-1 workflow: scaffold, requirements, PRD and stories, workplan, parallel lanes, QA, ship, feedback. Templates, a PRD-to-stories compiler, a stage detector, and two independent judge agents (prd-critic, story-verifier).
plugins.readme:
# foundry-sdlc

The deterministic 0-to-1 workflow AI Foundry uses to take software from an idea to a shipped, verified product with Claude Code agents. It has eight stages. Each stage produces one file and ends at a gate. A stage detector tells any agent which stage a project is in, so a new session (or a new teammate) picks up exactly where the last one stopped.

| # | Stage | Artifact | Item in this plugin |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | Scaffold | the artifact set | `new-project` skill, `scripts/new_project.py` |
| 1 | Gather requirements | `REQUIREMENTS.md`, `DECISIONS.md` | `gather-requirements` skill |
| 2 | PRD + user stories | `PRD.md`, `stories.json` | `write-prd` skill, `scripts/gen_stories.py`, `prd-critic` agent |
| 3 | Workplan | `WORKPLAN.md` | `write-workplan` skill |
| 4 | Execute | branches, one per lane | `parallel-lanes` skill |
| 5 | Code QA | tests, CI | (companion: `foundry-qa` regression-check) |
| 6 | Visual QA with example users | `done-journey.yaml`, screenshots | `story-verifier` agent (companions: `foundry-qa`, `foundry-design`, `foundry-devices`) |
| 7 | Ship | `CHANGELOG.md`, stories LIVE | `ship` skill |
| 8 | Feedback | new stories + failing tests | `bug-to-story` skill (companion: `foundry-evals`) |

The `sdlc` skill is the router. It holds the full map and the one rule that matters most: **never skip a gate**.

## Install

Add the marketplace once:

```text
/plugin marketplace add ai-foundry-byu/foundry-marketplace
```

Install this plugin:

```text
/plugin install foundry-sdlc@ai-foundry
```

From a shell instead (for example, to install for the whole project):

```bash
claude plugin install foundry-sdlc@ai-foundry --scope project
```

The companion plugins are installed the same way: `foundry-guardrails`, `foundry-qa`, `foundry-design`, `foundry-devices`, `foundry-evals`.

## Quick start

In your project, ask Claude: "Use foundry-sdlc to start a new project called Study Buddy." Or do it by hand:

```bash
python3 "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/new_project.py" product --name "Study Buddy" --owner "Team 4"
```

```bash
python3 "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/sdlc_stage.py" .
```

(`${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` is the plugin's install directory. If it is empty in your shell, the plugin lives at `$HOME/.claude/plugins/cache/ai-foundry/foundry-sdlc/<version>/`, or use your clone of this repo.) Then paste `docs/CLAUDE-md-snippet.md` into your project's `CLAUDE.md`.

## Items

### Skills

Invoke a skill by asking in plain words, for example "write the PRD", or by name: `/foundry-sdlc:write-prd`.

| Skill | What it does | Maturity |
|---|---|---|
| `sdlc` | The router. Stage map, which artifact and which skill or agent each stage uses, and how to detect the current stage | proven |
| `new-project` | Scaffolds the artifact set from `templates/`, copies `tools/gen_stories.py`, and sets up the CI check | proven |
| `gather-requirements` | Verbatim asks with R-ids and sources, a DECISIONS table, and an "Already exists" audit before the PRD | proven |
| `write-prd` | The PRD with inline `**US-01. Title.**` stories and observable criteria. Compiles stories.json, runs the prd-critic, and fills "Addressed critiques" | proven |
| `write-workplan` | Task table (Id, Task, Owner with model, effort and review tier by blast radius, Deps, Status), milestones, "Blocked on human" | proven |
| `parallel-lanes` | One git worktree and one agent per independent task: naming, the lane brief, the "edit only inside your worktree" rule, merge back | proven |
| `ship` | The ship ritual: done gate, persona testers, story-verifier, design review, then LIVE, changelog, and "go try X" | proven |
| `bug-to-story` | Each bug becomes a story plus a failing regression test. Usage gates, with graduation decided by a human | proven |

### Agents

| Agent | What it does | Maturity |
|---|---|---|
| `prd-critic` | Adversarial PRD review in a fresh context. Returns numbered critiques (C1..) with severity, location and a suggested fix. Read-only: never rewrites the PRD | proven (pattern) |
| `story-verifier` | Checks one story on the deployed build from its criteria, the URL and screenshots only. Returns PASS, FAIL or INCONCLUSIVE per criterion with evidence. Never reads the builder's claims | proven (pattern) |

Use them by asking, for example "Use the prd-critic agent on product/PRD.md", or let the `write-prd` and `ship` skills call them.

### Hook

| Hook | What it does | Maturity |
|---|---|---|
| SessionStart stage hint | Runs `sdlc_stage.py --hook`. If the project has a `PRD.md` or `REQUIREMENTS.md` (in the root, `product/` or `docs/product/`), it prints two lines: the current stage and the failing exit check. Silent otherwise. It never blocks a session | new |

### Scripts

| Script | What it does | Maturity |
|---|---|---|
| `scripts/gen_stories.py` | Compiles PRD stories into `stories.json`. `--check` exits 1 if the file is stale, a story has no criteria, an id is duplicated, or a status is invalid. Regenerating keeps `status`, `notes`, `evidence` and any meta the PRD does not set | proven (generalized port) |
| `scripts/new_project.py` | Scaffolds the artifact set. Never overwrites without `--force` | new |
| `scripts/sdlc_stage.py` | Reports the current stage from the files on disk (`--json` for machines, `--hook` for the SessionStart hook) | new |

### Templates and docs

| File | Purpose | Maturity |
|---|---|---|
| `templates/REQUIREMENTS.md` | Sources, verbatim asks (R-01..), "Already exists" audit, constraints, open questions | proven |
| `templates/DECISIONS.md` | Verbatim human decisions with what each one authorizes, and pending questions with a recommendation | proven |
| `templates/PRD.md` | Short version, user, metrics, principles, scope, stories, architecture, rollout with "used fully" gates, risks, Appendix A (addressed critiques), Appendix B (push back) | proven |
| `templates/WORKPLAN.md` | Status block, blast-radius tiers, Next up, milestones, task table, Blocked on human, Parked | proven |
| `templates/stories.schema.json` | JSON Schema for stories.json (id, title, acceptance[], surfaces[], devices[], status, waits_on[], optional covers/notes/evidence) | proven |
| `templates/done-journey.yaml` | Journey for the `foundry-qa` done gate: `steps` (goto, click, fill, wait_for), `assertions` (visible, text, url_contains), `screenshot` | proven (format) |
| `templates/CHANGELOG.md` | One dated heading per ship, one bullet per user-visible change, with evidence | proven |
| `templates/README.md` | Project README that indexes the artifact set | new |
| `docs/CLAUDE-md-snippet.md` | Always-on norms to paste into a project CLAUDE.md: root cause first, surgical changes, never "done" without a passing gate, the 4-tier blast-radius table, reuse before build | proven |

**What the maturity labels mean.** "proven" means the item is generalized from a workflow, format or tool that runs in production in our harness today. "proven (pattern)" means the agent's role and rules are what we use in production, rewritten here as a portable agent definition. "new" means it was written for this marketplace and is not yet battle-tested. Please report problems.

## Requirements

- Claude Code with plugin support.
- Python 3.8 or later for the scripts (standard library only).
- git 2.5 or later for worktrees (`parallel-lanes`).
- For `story-verifier` to drive a browser: Playwright for Python (`pip install playwright`, then `python3 -m playwright install chromium`). Without it, the verifier judges from screenshots and HTTP checks, and marks the rest INCONCLUSIVE.
- For stages 5 and 6: the companion plugins `foundry-qa` (done-gate, persona-tester, regression-check) and `foundry-design`. Native apps need `foundry-devices`.

## Tests

```bash
cd plugins/foundry-sdlc && python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts/tests -v
```

## Related work

Scott Murff's **agent-team-kit** (https://github.com/ai-foundry-byu/agent-team-kit) is a complementary team harness. It covers spec, mockup, build-spec, worktree launchers, merge-worktree, a regression check and release skills, installed with its own `install.sh`. This plugin does not copy any of its files. See its repository for license and usage.

## License

MIT. Copyright AI Foundry (BYU Marriott).

plugins.name: foundry-guardrails
plugins.description: Hooks that make the gates real: block destructive commands and secret leaks, require tests before done and before push or deploy, keep worktree sessions in their worktree, flag stale whole-file writes, and keep working until a workplan milestone is checked.
plugins.readme:
# foundry-guardrails

Claude Code hooks that turn SDLC rules from advice into gates. Your system prompt can *ask* Claude to run tests before saying "done", to stay out of `.env`, or to never force-push `main`. A hook *checks* it on every tool call and every stop, and it keeps checking when the session runs with skipped permission prompts.

Six hooks, all Python 3 standard library, all on by default except `ship-stop` (which turns on when you point it at a workplan):

| Hook | Event (matcher) | What it blocks | Default | Disable | Maturity |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `destructive-guard` | PreToolUse (`Bash`) | `rm -rf` of `/`, `~`, `$HOME`, `*`, `.` or a system dir; force-push to `main`/`master` (plain `--force` anywhere); `git reset --hard`, `git checkout -- .`, `git restore .`, `git clean -f` when they would destroy uncommitted work; `DROP`/`TRUNCATE`/`DELETE` without `WHERE` sent through a DB client; `dd of=/dev/...`; `mkfs`; fork bombs; `chmod -R 777 /`; `curl ... \| sh`; `shutdown`/`reboot` | deny | `FOUNDRY_DESTRUCTIVE_GUARD=0` | new |
| `secret-guard` | PreToolUse (`Bash\|Read\|Grep`) | Reading or printing `.env`, private keys, cloud/registry credential files; browser password and cookie stores; password-manager CLIs (`bw`, `op`, `lpass`, `pass`, `security ... -w`); token printers (`gh auth token`, `gcloud auth print-access-token`, ...); `env`/`printenv` dumps; `echo $API_KEY` | deny | `FOUNDRY_SECRET_GUARD=0` | proven |
| `verify-before-done` | PreToolUse (`Bash\|Edit\|Write\|MultiEdit\|NotebookEdit`) + Stop | Stopping after editing code with no test or typecheck run since the last edit (blocks once per stop, at most 2 times per session). Irreversible commands (`git push`, `vercel --prod`, `npm publish`, `wrangler deploy`, `terraform apply`, `gh pr merge`, ...) unless the command contains `VERIFY_OK=1` | on | `FOUNDRY_VERIFY=0` | proven |
| `worktree-guard` | PreToolUse (`Edit\|Write\|MultiEdit\|NotebookEdit`) | From inside a linked git worktree, editing a file in the main checkout | deny (only acts inside a linked worktree) | `FOUNDRY_WORKTREE_GUARD=0` | proven |
| `stale-write-guard` | PreToolUse (`Write`) | A whole-file `Write` to a git-tracked file that has uncommitted changes (they would be overwritten) | warn | `FOUNDRY_STALE_WRITE_GUARD=0` | new |
| `ship-stop` | Stop | Stopping while the workplan milestone you named is still `- [ ]` (at most 20 continuations per milestone) | off until `FOUNDRY_SHIP_WORKPLAN` is set | `FOUNDRY_SHIP_STOP=0` or unset the workplan | proven |
| `guardrails-help` | skill | Tells Claude how to respond when a guardrail blocks it, and tells you how to configure the hooks | n/a | n/a | new |

`FOUNDRY_GUARDRAILS=0` turns every hook off at once.

**Maturity.** "proven" means the hook is a generalized version of a hook that runs in our own Claude Code harness every day. "new" means it was written for this marketplace from documented patterns and is tested here, but it has not been run in daily use. `destructive-guard` uses the rule set of the published `claude-deploy-kit` command guard (a library, not a hook), so it is labeled new. `stale-write-guard` is ported from a guard we wrote but never switched on, so it is labeled new too.

## Guardrails, not a security boundary

These hooks catch the mistakes a well-meaning agent actually makes: running `cat .env` to "check the config", force-pushing over a teammate, wiping a directory with a bad glob, declaring victory without running tests. They are **not** a sandbox. A determined process can get around any pattern list. Shell writes (`cat > file`), scripts that read secrets from inside a file, and commands built at runtime are invisible to them. For a real boundary, use OS-level isolation: a container or VM, a scrubbed environment with no secrets in it, and least-privilege credentials. Use both.

## Install

Add the marketplace:

```text
/plugin marketplace add ai-foundry-byu/foundry-marketplace
```

Install the plugin:

```text
/plugin install foundry-guardrails@ai-foundry
```

Restart Claude Code so the hooks load. Then confirm they are registered:

```text
/hooks
```

To try it from a local clone without installing:

```bash
claude --plugin-dir ./plugins/foundry-guardrails
```

## Requirements

- `python3` (3.8 or newer) on your `PATH`. The hooks run in exec form (`python3 <script>`), so there is no shell quoting to break. If `python3` is missing, Claude Code treats each hook as a non-blocking error and the tool call goes ahead, so you lose the guard but your session keeps working.
- `git` for `destructive-guard` (dirty-tree checks), `worktree-guard` and `stale-write-guard`.
- macOS or Linux. Windows works when `python3` resolves to a real executable. Nothing here is tested on Windows yet.

## Configuration

Every switch is an environment variable. Put them in the `env` block of `.claude/settings.json` (project, shared with your team) or `.claude/settings.local.json` (just you), so the agent cannot change them from inside a command:

```json
{
  "env": {
    "FOUNDRY_STALE_WRITE_ENFORCE": "1",
    "FOUNDRY_VERIFY_IGNORE": "*.json,*.lock",
    "FOUNDRY_SHIP_WORKPLAN": "WORKPLAN.md",
    "FOUNDRY_SHIP_MILESTONE": "M3.2"
  }
}
```

| Variable | Hook | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `FOUNDRY_GUARDRAILS=0` | all | disable every hook |
| `FOUNDRY_DESTRUCTIVE_GUARD=0` | destructive-guard | disable |
| `FOUNDRY_DESTRUCTIVE_ALLOW=rule1,rule2` | destructive-guard | allow named rules for the session (rule names appear in every deny message, for example `git-reset-hard`) |
| `FOUNDRY_ALLOW_FORCE_PUSH=1` | destructive-guard | allow plain `--force` to non-protected branches. `main`/`master` stay blocked |
| `FOUNDRY_PROTECTED_BRANCHES=develop,release` | destructive-guard | add protected branches (`main` and `master` are always protected) |
| `FOUNDRY_SECRET_GUARD=0` | secret-guard | disable |
| `FOUNDRY_VERIFY=0` | verify-before-done | disable |
| `FOUNDRY_VERIFY_MAX_BLOCKS=2` | verify-before-done | Stop blocks allowed per session |
| `FOUNDRY_VERIFY_TEST_PATTERN='^just test'` | verify-before-done | extra regex that counts as a test command |
| `FOUNDRY_VERIFY_IRREVERSIBLE_PATTERN='^make release'` | verify-before-done | extra regex that needs `VERIFY_OK=1` |
| `FOUNDRY_VERIFY_IGNORE='*.json,config/*'` | verify-before-done | extra globs that do not count as code edits |
| `FOUNDRY_WORKTREE_GUARD=0` | worktree-guard | disable |
| `FOUNDRY_WORKTREE_GUARD_WARN=1` | worktree-guard | warn instead of deny |
| `FOUNDRY_STALE_WRITE_GUARD=0` | stale-write-guard | disable |
| `FOUNDRY_STALE_WRITE_ENFORCE=1` | stale-write-guard | deny instead of warn |
| `FOUNDRY_SHIP_WORKPLAN=path` | ship-stop | arm it (relative paths resolve from the project directory) |
| `FOUNDRY_SHIP_MILESTONE=M3.2` | ship-stop | the milestone to finish (default: the first open one) |
| `FOUNDRY_SHIP_MAX_BLOCKS=20` | ship-stop | continuation cap per milestone per session |
| `FOUNDRY_SHIP_STOP=0` | ship-stop | disable |
| `FOUNDRY_GUARDRAILS_STATE_DIR`, `FOUNDRY_GUARDRAILS_LOG` | all | override where state and the log go |

## How each hook behaves

### destructive-guard

Each command is normalized before matching. `sudo`, `env VAR=x`, `nohup`, `timeout`, `xargs` and leading `VAR=x` assignments are stripped. `bash -c '...'`, `sh -c`, `eval` and `$(...)` are unwrapped and checked as their own commands. Chains (`;`, `&&`, `||`, `|`) are split. Text inside a commit message or an `echo` is not a command, so `git commit -m "never rm -rf /"` is allowed.

Allowed on purpose, because blocking them would get the guard switched off: `rm -rf node_modules`, `rm -rf ./dist`, `git status`, `git push --force-with-lease` to a feature branch, `git reset --hard` on a clean tree, `DELETE FROM t WHERE ...`, `curl ... -o install.sh`.

Example deny, as Claude sees it:

```text
[foundry-guardrails/destructive-guard] Blocked destructive command (rule git-reset-hard):
git reset --hard would throw away uncommitted changes. Run git stash (recoverable) or
commit first. ...
```

SQL rules apply only when the command calls a database client (`psql`, `mysql`, `sqlite3`, `duckdb`, `supabase db`, `prisma db execute`, `wrangler d1 execute`, ...). An `echo "DROP TABLE"` is not blocked.

### secret-guard

Anything a command prints, or a file Claude reads, goes into the conversation and to the model provider. The guard denies the read or print, and points Claude at the safe forms:

| Allowed | Denied |
|---|---|
| `source .env && npm run dev` | `cat .env`, `head .env`, `grep KEY .env`, `Read(.env)` |
| `test -f .env`, `ls -la .env`, `grep -q KEY .env` | `echo $API_KEY`, `source .env && echo $DATABASE_URL` |
| `cp .env.example .env`, `cat .env.example` | `env`, `printenv`, `printenv OPENAI_API_KEY` |
| `docker run --env-file .env app` | `gh auth token`, `op read ...`, `security find-generic-password -w` |
| `cat ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub` | `cat ~/.ssh/id_ed25519`, `git show HEAD:.env` |

Secret files: `.env` and `.env.*` (but not `.env.example`, `.sample`, `.template`, `.dist`), `.envrc`, `*.pem`, `*.key`, `*.p12`, SSH private keys, `~/.aws/credentials`, `.netrc`, `.npmrc`, `.pypirc`, `.git-credentials`, docker and kube configs, the GitHub CLI hosts file, gcloud credentials, `credentials.json`, `service-account*.json`, `secrets.{json,yaml,toml}`.

### verify-before-done

1. Every `Edit`/`Write` to a code file inside the project marks the session "dirty" and clears "tested". Docs (`*.md`, `*.mdx`, `*.txt`, `*.rst`, `*.adoc`, anything under `docs/`) and files outside the project do not count.
2. A Bash test or typecheck marks it "tested": `pytest`, `python -m unittest`, `uv run pytest`, `npm test`, `npm run test:unit`, `pnpm typecheck`, `npx tsc --noEmit`, `vitest`, `jest`, `go test`, `cargo test`, `mvn test`, `gradle test`, `dotnet test`, `make test`, and more. The command has to start a stage, so `echo pytest` does not count.
3. On Stop: if the session is dirty and untested, Claude gets one block with this reason, then continues:

   ```text
   [foundry-guardrails/verify-before-done] You edited 2 code file(s) (app.py, api.py) and no test
   or typecheck command has run since the last edit. Before finishing: run the project's tests or
   typecheck ..., and report the command and its result. If this change cannot be tested, say so
   plainly and explain why. (block 1 of at most 2 this session; FOUNDRY_VERIFY=0 disables)
   ```

4. It cannot loop. When Claude stops again while `stop_hook_active` is true, the stop is allowed and an "unverified stop" line is logged. The session-wide cap (default 2) and Claude Code's own limit of 8 consecutive continuations back that up. While background tasks are still running (a test run in the background, for example), the stop is allowed and the session stays dirty.
5. Irreversible commands are denied until the command carries `VERIFY_OK=1`, for example `VERIFY_OK=1 git push origin feature`. The token is logged and also counts as verification for the Stop check. It is an explicit claim that the agent verified the work, and it shows up in review. It is not a lock.

### worktree-guard

When the session's working directory is inside a linked worktree (`git worktree add`, or Claude Code's own worktrees), an edit through an absolute path into the main checkout is denied, and the reason names the same file inside your worktree. Edits inside your worktree, to `/tmp`, to another repo, or to another worktree are allowed. In the main checkout the hook does nothing.

### stale-write-guard

A `Write` replaces the whole file with what Claude holds in context. If the tracked file has uncommitted changes (from you, a formatter, or another session), the hook warns Claude by default. The warning goes into Claude's context and the write still happens. With `FOUNDRY_STALE_WRITE_ENFORCE=1` it denies the write and tells Claude to read the file again and use `Edit`. New files, untracked files, files outside git, clean files and identical content always pass.

### ship-stop

Keeps Claude working until a milestone in your workplan is checked off. The workplan format:

```markdown
- [x] M3.1 Schema migration
- [ ] M3.2 Export endpoint returns CSV
  - acceptance: GET /export?fmt=csv returns 200 with a header row
  - acceptance: pytest tests/test_export.py passes
- [!] M3.3 Payment webhook (blocked: needs a sandbox key from a human)
```

- `- [ ]` is open, `- [x]` is done, and `- [!]` or `- [-]` is blocked or deferred, with the reason on the same line. Only an open milestone blocks.
- Indented lines under a milestone are quoted back to Claude as its acceptance notes.
- After 20 continuations on one milestone (`FOUNDRY_SHIP_MAX_BLOCKS`), the stop is allowed and stderr says a human needs to look.
- A missing file, an unknown milestone id, or background tasks still running all allow the stop.

Arm it for one run:

```bash
FOUNDRY_SHIP_WORKPLAN=WORKPLAN.md FOUNDRY_SHIP_MILESTONE=M3.2 claude
```

## State and logs

Per-session markers and the log go in `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA}/state/` when Claude Code provides it, and otherwise in `${TMPDIR}/foundry-guardrails/`. Every deny, warning, Stop block and unverified stop is one JSON line in `guardrails.log`:

```json
{"ts": "2026-10-28T07:40:46", "hook": "secret-guard", "action": "deny", "session": "abc123", "tool": "Bash", "reason": "Blocked: this command prints a dotenv file (.env). ...", "command": "cat .env"}
```

Read it to see what the agent tried, and to tune false positives.

## Failure behavior

Every hook **fails open**. Malformed stdin, a missing `git`, an unwritable state directory or a bug in the hook itself leads to exit 0 with no output, so the tool call goes ahead and an `error-fail-open` line is logged. A broken guard must never brick a session. The cost is that a broken guard is silent, so check the log after you change a hook.

## Tests

```bash
cd plugins/foundry-guardrails
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v
```

88 tests. They cover the allow and deny cases for each rule, the false positives listed above, malformed stdin, the disable switches, the Stop loop caps, and real temporary git repos and worktrees. The hooks were also checked end to end in a live `claude -p --plugin-dir` session: `cat .env` was denied, and a code edit with no tests got exactly one Stop block.

## Known limitations

- Pattern matching cannot see inside script files. `python leak.py` that prints `.env`, or `psql -f drop.sql`, is not caught.
- `verify-before-done` sees that a test command *ran*, not that it *passed*. The Stop message asks Claude to report the result. Review it.
- `VERIFY_OK=1` can be typed by the agent itself. It is an audit token, not an approval. If you need a human approval step, deny the command and have the human run it.
- `secret-guard` denies `sed -i` on `.env` (a reader command naming a secret file). Edit `.env` yourself.
- The worktree guard only sees the `Edit`/`Write`/`NotebookEdit` tools, not shell writes.
- `stale-write-guard` warns whenever a tracked file is dirty, including when the dirt is Claude's own earlier edit in the same session. That is why it warns by default.

## Credits

These hooks are small, self-contained versions of two fuller MIT-licensed projects. Use those when you need more:

- [ethos-gate](https://github.com/jddavenportOpen/ethos-gate): irreversible-action guard, credential-scrape policy with strict and sandbox tiers, an outbound GitHub action gate with an LLM judge, and a lethal-trifecta audit.
- [claude-deploy-kit](https://github.com/jddavenportOpen/claude-deploy-kit): the destructive command rule set, policy and eval gates, and the audit trail for fleets of headless agents.

For a full team harness (agents, skills, memory, hooks) built for the AI Foundry cohort, see [agent-team-kit](https://github.com/ai-foundry-byu/agent-team-kit).

## License

MIT. See [LICENSE](LICENSE).

plugins.name: foundry-qa
plugins.description: Web QA: a definition-of-done gate (deployed SHA plus a Playwright journey on desktop, phone and tablet), blast-radius regression checks, axe-core accessibility, screenshot baselines, and web-qa, persona-tester and explorer agents.
plugins.readme:
# foundry-qa

Web QA for Claude Code, in code and with example users. It gives your agent a strict
definition of done, a way to find what a change could break, accessibility and visual
regression checks, and three QA agents that drive your app in a real browser.

Part of the [AI Foundry marketplace](https://github.com/ai-foundry-byu/foundry-marketplace).

## Install

Add the marketplace (once):

```text
/plugin marketplace add ai-foundry-byu/foundry-marketplace
```

Install the plugin:

```text
/plugin install foundry-qa@ai-foundry
```

Install the browser tooling the scripts use (once per machine):

```bash
pip install playwright
```

```bash
python3 -m playwright install chromium
```

Optional, for Safari-engine runs:

```bash
python3 -m playwright install webkit
```

## What is in it

| Item | Type | What it does | SDLC stage | Maturity |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `done-gate` | skill | Definition-of-done gate: deployed SHA check, then a Playwright journey on each device, strict exit codes | ship / verify | proven |
| `regression-check` | skill | Stack-neutral blast-radius method: grep every consumer, judge each, behavior-test the at-risk ones | build / verify | proven |
| `a11y-check` | skill | axe-core in a real browser plus a manual WCAG 2.2 AA floor checklist | verify | proven |
| `visual-baseline` | skill | Screenshot baselines, pixel diff with threshold and tolerance, deliberate approve step | verify | proven |
| `web-qa` | agent | Drives the app with Playwright: journeys, a11y, visual, console and network errors, mobile emulation; files findings with repro steps | verify | proven |
| `persona-tester` | agent | Tests every user story as a persona across device profiles, read-only by default; reports judged versus passed; tickets repeated failures | verify / user acceptance | proven |
| `explorer` | agent | Curious-human crawler plus a manual probe list: edge cases, empty states, Back, refresh, double submit | verify | proven (pattern) |
| `scripts/done_gate.py` | script | The gate itself (journey runner, SHA check, read-only guard) | ship / verify | proven |
| `scripts/persona_run.py` | script | Persona story runner with persona checks and ticket filing | verify | proven |
| `scripts/a11y_check.py` | script | axe-core runner | verify | proven |
| `scripts/visual_baseline.py` | script | capture / compare / check / approve | verify | proven |
| `scripts/explore.py` | script | Same-origin read-only crawler | verify | proven (pattern) |
| `scripts/qa_yaml.py` | script | Dependency-free YAML subset parser so students do not need PyYAML | support | new |
| `templates/done-journey.yaml` | template | Annotated journey to copy into your repo | ship | new |
| `templates/stories.example.json` | template | Example user stories for persona runs | requirements / verify | new |
| `templates/personas/*.md` | template | Persona template plus two examples: first-time mobile user, power user on desktop | requirements / verify | new |

### What "maturity" means here

- **proven**: generalized from a tool that runs in production in our own Claude Code harness
  today. The method and the exit-code contracts come from that tool. The code in this plugin is
  a fresh, dependency-light rewrite of it for public use, tested against a fixture site in a
  real browser (see Tests below).
- **proven (pattern)**: the approach runs in production in our harness; this version's
  details (the crawl signals and probe list) were written for this marketplace.
- **new**: written for this marketplace from documentation and best practice, not yet
  battle-tested.

## How to use each item

### done-gate (skill)

Ask: "run the done gate on the signup feature" or "is this done? prove it". The skill walks
the agent through writing `qa/done-journey.yaml` and running:

```bash
python3 "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/done_gate.py" --journey qa/done-journey.yaml --base-url http://localhost:3000
```

Against a deployed build, with the commit check and production-safe read-only mode:

```bash
python3 "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/done_gate.py" --journey qa/done-journey.yaml \
  --base-url https://<your-app>.example.com \
  --sha-url https://<your-app>.example.com/api/version --sha-json-key commit --read-only
```

Exit codes: `0` pass, `1` journey fail, `2` config error, `3` SHA mismatch, `6` inconclusive.
**Only say "done" on exit 0. Inconclusive is not a pass.** Evidence goes to `.qa/done-gate/`.

Journey format (YAML subset or JSON):

```yaml
steps:
  - goto: /
  - click: "text=Get started"
  - fill: {selector: "#email", value: "qa@example.com"}
  - press: {selector: "#email", key: "Enter"}
  - wait_for: "[data-testid=dashboard]"
assertions:
  - visible: "[data-testid=dashboard]"
  - text: {selector: "h1", contains: "Welcome"}
  - url_contains: /dashboard
  - no_console_errors: true
screenshot: signup
devices: [desktop-1440x900, phone-390x844, tablet-820x1180]
```

### regression-check (skill)

Ask: "what could this change break?" or "run a regression check before we merge". The agent
lists what changed, greps every consumer, writes a consumer table with an at-risk verdict for
each, and runs the smallest test that proves each at-risk consumer still works. This method
comes from Scott Murff's
[agent-team-kit](https://github.com/ai-foundry-byu/agent-team-kit) (`skills/regression-check`),
which is written for a SvelteKit project; this is a stack-neutral version.

### a11y-check (skill)

Ask: "check accessibility on the signup page".

```bash
python3 "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/a11y_check.py" --url http://localhost:3000/signup --devices desktop-1440x900,phone-390x844
```

Exit `0` clean at `--fail-on serious`, `1` blocking violations, `2` config, `6` inconclusive.
Then the agent walks the manual WCAG 2.2 AA checklist in the skill (keyboard, focus, labels,
contrast, zoom, target size, motion).

### visual-baseline (skill)

Ask: "check for visual regressions on home and pricing".

```bash
python3 "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/visual_baseline.py" check --url http://localhost:3000/ --name home --devices desktop-1440x900,phone-390x844
```

First run exits `6` (no baselines). Look at `.qa/visual/current/`, then `approve`. After that,
`check` exits `1` on a diff over threshold and writes red-highlight images to `.qa/visual/diff/`.

### web-qa (agent)

Ask: "use web-qa to QA the checkout flow on localhost" or "QA prod after the deploy
(read-only)". It plans journeys from your acceptance criteria, runs journeys, axe, visual and
a crawl, reads the screenshots, re-runs failures, and files findings with numbered repro steps
in `.qa/findings.md`.

### persona-tester (agent)

Copy the templates into your project:

```bash
mkdir -p qa/personas && cp "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}"/templates/personas/*.md qa/personas/ && cp "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/templates/stories.example.json" qa/stories.json
```

Edit them to match your real users and stories, then ask: "use persona-tester to test every
story as the first-time mobile user on staging". Under the hood:

```bash
python3 "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/persona_run.py" --persona qa/personas/first-time-mobile-user.md --stories qa/stories.json --base-url <url>
```

It is **read-only by default**: every POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE is answered inside the browser and
never sent, so it is safe against production. `--allow-writes` is refused for anything but
localhost. It reports `passed`, `failed`, `needs-judgment` and `inconclusive` separately, and
the agent labels its own screenshot judgments JUDGED, never passed. `--file-tickets` writes a
ticket only for failures seen on two runs in a row.

### explorer (agent)

Ask: "use explorer to find bugs on localhost:3000". It runs the read-only crawler:

```bash
python3 "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/explore.py" --url http://localhost:3000 --max-pages 30
```

then probes by hand (Back, refresh mid-flow, double submit, odd input, slow network, empty
states), with submit and double-submit probes only on local or staging.

### Running the scripts without the plugin (CI)

`${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` is filled in by Claude Code inside skills and agents. In CI or a plain
terminal, copy the `scripts/` folder into your repo (for example `qa/tools/`) and call it
there:

```bash
python3 qa/tools/done_gate.py --journey qa/done-journey.yaml --base-url "$PREVIEW_URL" --read-only
```

## Requirements

- Python 3.9 or newer. Standard library only, except Playwright for anything that opens a browser.
- Playwright for Python and a browser build (`python3 -m playwright install chromium`).
- `a11y_check.py` downloads a pinned axe-core build from cdnjs once (cached in `.qa/cache/`),
  or uses a local file via `--axe-source`.
- Optional: Pillow speeds up decoding of very large screenshots. Not required.
- Add `.qa/` to your project's `.gitignore` (screenshots can contain real data). Commit
  `.qa/visual/baselines/` only if you want baselines in git; otherwise point `--root` elsewhere.

## Tests

From the plugin directory:

```bash
cd tests && python3 -m unittest -v
```

The unit tests (YAML parser, journey validation, SHA extraction and matching, the exit-code
contract, PNG codec, pixel diff, persona and story parsing, read-only rules, ticket logic,
crawler URL rules) need no browser. `test_browser_integration.py` starts a local fixture site
and runs every script in headless Chromium; it skips itself if Playwright or Chromium is not
installed, and the a11y case skips if axe-core cannot be downloaded.

## Known limitations

- The YAML parser is a subset: no block scalars (`|`, `>`), anchors or tags. Quote selectors.
  Use JSON if you prefer.
- `--read-only` answers blocked writes with a fake `200 {"qaReadOnly": true}`. Apps that expect
  a specific response shape may show an error state instead of success. Either way, a simulated
  write proves only that the UI responded.
- The read-only guard sees HTTP requests the page makes. It cannot stop writes sent over
  WebSockets or by a service worker that was already installed, or server-side effects of a GET.
  Never rely on it alone against a production app that changes data on GET.
- Device profiles emulate viewport, touch and user agent in Chromium. They are not real devices.
  Run `--browser webkit` for Safari-engine behavior, and test on a real phone before launch.
- Visual baselines are sensitive to OS fonts and browser version. Capture baselines and checks
  in the same environment.
- axe-core catches only part of WCAG. The manual checklist is not optional.
- The persona judgments are an agent's reading of screenshots. They are labeled JUDGED for a
  reason: they are not a substitute for watching real users.

## License

MIT. Copyright AI Foundry, BYU Marriott School of Business.

plugins.name: foundry-design
plugins.description: Design gates: a subtract-only design critic, a UI spec writer with a full state matrix and checkable acceptance criteria, a design-system template, a read-only ui-reviewer agent, and a deterministic design gate script.
plugins.readme:
# foundry-design

Design quality gates for Claude Code. Agents are good at generating screens and bad at editing
them: they ship features that pass every functional test while the experience gets worse (an
extra step, a dead button, a second panel that does the same job, gray-on-gray text). This
plugin adds the missing editor, a spec step before the build, and a scored review after it.

| Item | Type | What it does | SDLC stage | Maturity |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `design-critique` | skill | Subtract-only critic: 8-question constitution (C1-C8), findings schema, four-tier resolver, decision log | build (pre-build) and visual QA | proven |
| `ui-ux-spec` | skill | Turns a user story into a buildable UI spec: layout per breakpoint, full state matrix, keyboard and touch, copy, tokens, machine-checkable acceptance checks | design / pre-build | proven |
| `design-system` | skill | Fill-in template for your design system (tokens, contrast table, type scale, spacing, components, vocabulary) that the other items grade against | design | new |
| `ui-reviewer` | agent | Read-only REVIEW: scores screenshots plus code on a 10-dimension 0-4 rubric, returns token-level must-fixes with file:line. Never edits source | visual QA / ship | proven |
| `design_gate.py` | script | Deterministic gate: clicks-to-goal, dead controls, entry points, primary buttons, tap targets, contrast, horizontal scroll, context present; fails on regression vs a baseline | visual QA / CI | new (generalized from a proven per-project gate) |
| `validate_findings.py` | script | Validates a critique findings file: no "add" verb, deltas on flow findings, nit cap, grounding | visual QA | new |
| `design-gate.config.json`, `findings.example.json`, `decision.yaml` | templates | Starting files for the gate config, a findings run, and a decision-log entry | setup | new |

Maturity: **proven** means generalized from a tool that runs in production in our harness today.
**new** means written for this marketplace from docs and best practice, not yet battle-tested.
`design_gate.py` is the generalized form of a gate that runs in production for one of our apps;
the generic config-driven version, the contrast and target checks, and the validator are new.

## Install

Add the marketplace:

```
/plugin marketplace add ai-foundry-byu/foundry-marketplace
```

Install the plugin:

```
/plugin install foundry-design@ai-foundry
```

Reload so the skills and agent appear (or restart Claude Code):

```
/reload-plugins
```

To try it from a local clone without installing:

```bash
claude --plugin-dir ./plugins/foundry-design
```

## How the pieces fit

```
user story -> ui-ux-spec (spec + acceptance checks)
           -> design-critique pre-build (C3/C5/C6/C8 on the plan)
           -> build
           -> design_gate.py (objective numbers, hard-fails regressions)
           -> ui-reviewer agent (scored rubric, must-fixes)
           -> design-critique post-build (subtract-only pass, decision log)
           -> ship
```

All project state lives in a `design/` directory at your repo root:

```
design/
  design-system.md        # from the design-system skill
  vocabulary.md           # one name per act
  core-flows.md           # the 1-3 jobs that matter, as steps
  design-gate.json        # gate config (copy templates/design-gate.config.json)
  design-baseline.json    # written by the gate's bless command, committed
  specs/<surface>.md      # from ui-ux-spec
  reviews/                # ui-reviewer reports and captures
  findings/               # design-critique runs (JSON arrays)
  decisions/              # one YAML per ruling
  references/             # pinned good-*.png / bad-*.png examples
```

## Using each item

### design-critique (skill, proven)

Ask: "run the design critique on the settings page" or `/foundry-design:design-critique`.
Pre-build it critiques the plan; post-build it runs the gate, then examines every changed screen
against C1-C8 and writes a findings file. The critic may only propose `remove`, `merge`,
`relabel`, `inline` or `escalate`. Validate the findings:

```bash
python3 "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/validate_findings.py" design/findings/2026-01-15-settings.json
```

`${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` is set for hooks and expanded in plugin content, but not in your own
terminal. From a terminal, locate the script:

```bash
find "$HOME/.claude/plugins" -path '*foundry-design/scripts/*' -name '*.py' 2>/dev/null
```

For CI, copy `scripts/design_gate.py` and `scripts/validate_findings.py` into your repo (MIT).

### ui-ux-spec (skill, proven)

Ask: "spec the checkout screen from story US-14" or `/foundry-design:ui-ux-spec`. It fills
`references/spec-template.md` into `design/specs/<surface>.md`, self-checks against
`references/floor-checklist.md`, and maps its acceptance checks to gate metrics.

### design-system (skill, new)

Ask: "set up our design system" or `/foundry-design:design-system`. It inventories the raw
values your code actually uses, collapses them into tokens, measures contrast for every
text/background pair, and writes `design/design-system.md` from the template. For choosing an
aesthetic direction on a greenfield product, use Anthropic's official `frontend-design` skill from
the `claude-plugins-official` marketplace; this plugin does not copy it.

### ui-reviewer (agent, proven)

Ask: "have the ui-reviewer score the dashboard against design/specs/dashboard.md". It captures
screenshots (via the gate or Playwright), reads the code, scores 10 dimensions 0-4, and returns a
verdict (`SHIP`, `SHIP AFTER MUST-FIXES`, `REWORK`, `REDESIGN`) with must-fixes that each carry
evidence, problem, a token-level fix and a verification step. It writes only under
`design/reviews/` and never edits product source. The rubric is
`skills/ui-ux-spec/references/rubric.md`.

### design_gate.py (script, new)

1. Install Playwright (only the measuring step needs it):

   ```bash
   python3 -m pip install playwright
   python3 -m playwright install chromium
   ```

2. Copy `templates/design-gate.config.json` to `design/design-gate.json` and edit `base_url`,
   `pages`, `flows` (click steps to a goal selector), `context_checks` and
   `selectors.primary_button`.
3. Start your app locally, then establish the baseline and commit it:

   ```bash
   python3 path/to/design_gate.py run --config design/design-gate.json --bless
   ```

4. On every UI change:

   ```bash
   python3 path/to/design_gate.py run --config design/design-gate.json
   ```

Exit codes: 0 pass, 1 regression or hard-limit violation, 2 config error, 3 refused a
non-local `base_url` (flows can write data, so the gate only drives localhost unless you set
`"allow_remote": true` for a read-only target).

Hard limits (fail even without a baseline, each can be set to `null` to rely on the baseline
only, which helps when adopting the gate on an existing app): one primary button per screen,
no horizontal scroll, zero targets under 44 px (touch) or 24 px (pointer), zero text under
4.5:1 (3:1 large), zero unlabeled buttons, every core flow reaches its goal. Regressions against
the baseline: any increase in clicks, dead controls, entry points or the counts above, any
context check or flow that stops holding, and any metric that disappears.

`check` and `bless` are stdlib only, so a collector in another language can write the metrics
JSON and reuse the comparison:

```bash
python3 design_gate.py check --current metrics.json --baseline design/design-baseline.json
```

Keep the gate honest: plant a known-bad on a branch (an extra click, a disabled button, a second
primary) and confirm the gate exits 1. The unit tests do exactly this.

## Tests

```bash
cd plugins/foundry-design
python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts/tests -v
```

44 tests: color math and WCAG contrast, page evaluation, hard limits, planted regressions,
config validation, the CLI, the findings validator, and one end-to-end Playwright run against a
local fixture page (skipped when Playwright or Chromium is not installed).

## Requirements

- Claude Code with plugin support.
- Python 3.9+ (stdlib) for the scripts.
- Playwright for Python plus a Chromium (or WebKit) build, only for `design_gate.py measure|run`
  and for the reviewer's own captures.

## Known limitations

- Contrast is computed from computed `color` and `background-color` only. Text over background
  images or gradients is counted as unknown, and element `opacity` and `mix-blend-mode` are
  ignored. Check those by eye.
- Clicks-to-goal counts the `click` steps you wrote in the config; it does not discover a shorter
  path. Keep flows written as the real user path.
- `entry_points` and `primary_buttons` depend on your selectors; a wrong selector silently counts
  0 (an invalid selector counts -1).
- The reviewer's screen-reader and latency claims are judgment, not measurement, unless you add
  tests for them; the agent labels them so.
- The design system template is a starting point, not a token pipeline: it does not generate CSS.

## License

MIT. Grounding references (WCAG, Nielsen heuristics, platform guidelines) are cited by link; no
third-party text is vendored.

plugins.name: foundry-devices
plugins.description: Native and desktop QA agents for iOS Simulator, Android, Windows and macOS, plus a device-matrix skill that runs them as parallel lanes and merges one PASS/FAIL/INCONCLUSIVE matrix.
plugins.readme:
# foundry-devices Native and device QA agents, one per platform, so you can grab the one for your target. Each agent is an operating manual that a Claude Code subagent follows: prerequisites, a doctor check it runs first, a drive loop (launch, act, screenshot, read the UI tree, assert, repeat), evidence capture to `.qa//`, and a report with PASS, FAIL or INCONCLUSIVE per user story. ## Honest status: read this first Everything in this plugin is **new**. It was written for this marketplace from official documentation (Apple simctl and System Events, Android SDK, Maestro, pywinauto, Playwright) and best practice. It is **not** generalized from a tool we run in production. What we do run in production today, for comparison: - A **real iPhone** driver (iPhone Mirroring on a Mac). That one is proven and lives in its own plugin, **foundry-iphone-mirror**. Use it for stories that need real hardware. - **Playwright mobile emulation** for web apps, in the **foundry-qa** plugin. We have nothing proven for the iOS Simulator, Android native, Windows desktop or macOS desktop apps. These agents are our best written plan for those targets. **If you use one, please report back** (open an issue or a pull request on the marketplace repo) with what worked, what broke, and the exact tool versions. Two or three good field reports and we will promote an item to proven. ## Install Add the marketplace (once): ```text /plugin marketplace add ai-foundry-byu/foundry-marketplace ``` Install this plugin: ```text /plugin install foundry-devices@ai-foundry ``` From a shell instead of a session: ```bash claude plugin install foundry-devices@ai-foundry --scope project ``` ## What is inside | item | type | what it does | SDLC stage | maturity | |---|---|---|---|---| | `ios-qa` | agent | iOS Simulator QA: simctl boot/install/launch/openurl/screenshot/recordVideo/privacy/status_bar, Maestro flows, optional XCUITest | QA / verify | new | | `android-qa` | agent | Android QA: AVD + emulator, adb install/am start/input/screencap, uiautomator UI tree, logcat crashes, dumpsys, Maestro, optional Appium | QA / verify | new | | `windows-qa` | agent | Windows desktop QA: pywinauto UIA backend, find by automation id/name, invoke/type, control tree, screenshots, event log; Playwright for web, WinAppDriver/Appium optional | QA / verify | new | | `macos-qa` | agent | macOS desktop QA: System Events accessibility tree, AXPress, keystroke, screencapture, cliclick, Playwright `_electron` for Electron apps | QA / verify | new | | `device-matrix` | skill | choose device lanes from each story's `devices[]`, run them in parallel, merge one matrix and verdict | QA / plan + report | new | | `scripts/doctor.py` | script | preflight per platform (tools present and responding, host OS, permissions), writes `.qa//doctor.json` | QA / setup | new (unit-tested) | | `scripts/uitree.py` | script | read an Android `uiautomator dump`: outline, find by text/id/desc, print a safe `adb shell input tap` for exactly one match | QA / drive | new (unit-tested) | | `scripts/ax_tree.py` | script | dump, outline, search and AXPress a macOS app's accessibility tree; window bounds for screenshots | QA / drive | new (parsing unit-tested) | | `scripts/device_matrix.py` | script | `plan`, `init`, `report` for the device matrix | QA / plan + report | new (unit-tested) | | `templates/maestro/android-sign-in.yaml` | template | Maestro sign-in flow for Android | QA / drive | new | | `templates/maestro/ios-sign-in.yaml` | template | Maestro sign-in flow for the iOS Simulator | QA / drive | new | | `templates/stories.example.json` | template | stories with `devices[]` | QA / plan | new | | `templates/results.example.json` | template | the per-lane results file every agent writes | QA / report | new | | `templates/matrix.template.md` | template | what a finished matrix looks like | QA / report | new | There are no hooks in this plugin. Nothing runs unless you ask for it. ## How to use each item ### The agents Ask for them by name or by task. Claude Code picks the agent from its description, or you can name it: ```text Use the android-qa agent to test story S1 in stories.json against app/build/outputs/apk/debug/app-debug.apk with the test account in QA_EMAIL / QA_PASSWORD. ``` Every agent does the same four things in order: 1. **Doctor**: runs `scripts/doctor.py --platform

` and reports READY or the exact fixes. It stops if not ready. 2. **Drive loop** per story: arrange a clean state, act through the UI tree (never guessed coordinates), wait for a condition, screenshot, assert, and look at the screenshot itself. 3. **Evidence** under `.qa//`, named `--.png` plus tree dumps and logs. 4. **Report**: `.qa//results.json` plus a short table. PASS needs evidence, FAIL needs a reproduction note and logs, INCONCLUSIVE says what blocked it. All agents follow the same safety rules: test accounts and test data only, never production or a real person's account unless you say so in the task, never erase devices or simulators they did not create, secrets only through environment variables. ### The device-matrix skill ```text /foundry-devices:device-matrix ``` Or just say "run the device matrix for stories.json". The skill walks through: ```bash python3 "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/device_matrix.py" plan stories.json python3 "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/device_matrix.py" init stories.json --qa .qa # ... one subagent per lane, in parallel ... python3 "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/device_matrix.py" report stories.json --qa .qa # exit 0 PASS, 1 FAIL, 3 INCONCLUSIVE ``` ### The scripts on their own All scripts are Python 3 standard library only and print `--help`. ```bash python3 scripts/doctor.py --platform android python3 scripts/uitree.py tap .qa/android/ui.xml --text "Sign in" --exact --clickable python3 scripts/ax_tree.py dump "Calculator" --depth 6 --out .qa/macos/ax.json ``` ## Requirements | lane | host | install | |---|---|---| | ios-qa | macOS | Xcode (open it once, accept the license, install an iOS runtime); Maestro: `curl -fsSL "https://get.maestro.mobile.dev" \| bash`; a JDK 17+ for Maestro | | android-qa | macOS, Linux or Windows | Android SDK platform-tools, emulator, cmdline-tools (via Android Studio or `sdkmanager`); Maestro optional; Appium optional (`npm i -g appium`, `appium driver install uiautomator2`) | | windows-qa | native Windows 10/11 (not WSL) | Python 3, `py -m pip install pywinauto pillow`; Playwright optional for web | | macos-qa | macOS | Accessibility and Screen Recording permission for the app running Claude Code; `brew install cliclick` optional; Node + `npm i -D playwright` for Electron apps | | device-matrix | any | Python 3 | ## Tests ```bash cd plugins/foundry-devices python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v ``` The tests cover the logic in the scripts (UI tree parsing and matching, the tap ambiguity guard, matrix planning and verdict rules, doctor timeouts and adb parsing). They do not start a simulator, emulator or desktop app. ## Known limitations - None of the drive loops have been run end to end by us on real projects yet. Expect some commands to need adjusting for your tool versions. Each agent tells you to check the tool's own `--help` and to note differences in its report. - `xcrun simctl` subcommand options (for example `privacy` service names) change between Xcode releases. - `ax_tree.py dump` can be slow on large windows and needs the Accessibility permission; paths go stale as soon as the UI changes. - Windows automation needs an active, unlocked desktop session, cannot cross the UAC secure desktop, and cannot drive an elevated app from a non-elevated script. - Apps that draw their own UI (games, some cross-platform toolkits) expose little to any accessibility tree, so agents fall back to screenshots and coordinates with lower confidence. ## License MIT.

plugins.name: foundry-iphone-mirror
plugins.description: Drive a real iPhone from a Mac through macOS iPhone Mirroring: screenshot, read, tap, type, swipe, verify. A skill, an iphone-driver agent, an MCP server and a CLI with a doctor.
plugins.readme:
# foundry-iphone-mirror

Drive a real iPhone from your Mac with Claude Code. The plugin uses macOS **iPhone
Mirroring**: it screenshots the mirrored phone, lets the model read the screenshot,
injects one tap, swipe or keystroke, and screenshots again to verify. Use it for
real-device QA of your iOS app and for any on-phone task that has no Mac-side API.

It is the only real-device iOS path in this marketplace. It does not use the iOS
Simulator, XCUITest or Appium, and it does not need a developer account or a cable.

## What's inside

| Item | Type | What it gives you | Maturity |
|---|---|---|---|
| `iphone-mirror` | skill | the screenshot, read, act, verify loop, command reference, recipes, rules | proven |
| `iphone-driver` | agent | delegate a whole on-phone task; screenshots stay in its context, you get the outcome | proven |
| `iphone-mirror` | script (CLI, on PATH) | `doctor`, `build`, `open`, `shot`, `tap`, `swipe`, `type`, `key`, `home`, `info`, `tapxy`, `map` | proven |
| `engine/worker.sh` + `engine/launcher.c` | script | the privileged worker and the Mach-O launcher sealed inside the helper app | proven |
| `engine/build-helper-app.sh` | script | builds, ad hoc signs and registers the helper app | proven |
| `iphone` | MCP server (`mcp/server.py`) | typed `iphone_*` tools; `iphone_screenshot` returns the PNG inline | new |

**What the labels mean.** "proven" means generalized from a tool that runs in
production in our own harness today, driving a real iPhone. "new" means written for this marketplace and not yet battle-tested.
The MCP server is new because it is a rewrite: our production server uses the `mcp`
Python package, and this one is standard-library only so you install nothing. Its tool
surface is the same, and it is covered by protocol tests, but it has not driven a
phone in our harness yet. The port also changed the engine in small ways (listed under
"Changes from the source" below) that are unit-tested but not yet re-run on a device.

## Requirements

- macOS 15 (Sequoia) or newer, with the **iPhone Mirroring** app. Not offered in every
  region (it has been unavailable in the EU).
- An iPhone on iOS 18 or newer, signed in to the same Apple Account as the Mac, nearby,
  with Wi-Fi and Bluetooth on. Pair it once by opening iPhone Mirroring and following
  the prompts.
- Xcode Command Line Tools for `clang` (one-time, to build the helper app):
  `xcode-select --install`
- `cliclick` for clicks and keystrokes: `brew install cliclick`
- Python 3 (any 3.8+) for the MCP server. Standard library only.

## Install

Add the marketplace:

```text
/plugin marketplace add ai-foundry-byu/foundry-marketplace
```

Install the plugin:

```text
/plugin install foundry-iphone-mirror@ai-foundry
```

Then restart Claude Code so the skill, agent, CLI and MCP server load.

From a shell instead:

```bash
claude plugin install foundry-iphone-mirror@ai-foundry
```

## One-time setup (about 5 minutes)

**1. Install the tools.**

```bash
xcode-select --install
brew install cliclick
```

**2. Build the helper app.** This compiles a tiny launcher, copies the worker into an
app bundle, signs it ad hoc and registers it. Default location
`$HOME/Applications/FoundryPhone.app`.

```bash
iphone-mirror build
```

Options: `--app PATH` (must end in `.app`), `--bundle-id ID`, `--name NAME`. The chosen
path is remembered in `$HOME/Library/Application Support/foundry-iphone-mirror/helper-path`,
so the CLI and the MCP server find it without environment variables.

If `iphone-mirror` is not on your PATH (for example in a plain terminal outside Claude
Code), run it by full path from the plugin directory, `<plugin-dir>/bin/iphone-mirror`.
`claude plugin details foundry-iphone-mirror` shows where the plugin is installed.

**3. Open iPhone Mirroring and connect the phone.**

```bash
iphone-mirror open
```

Unlock or approve on the phone if asked. Keep the Mirroring window on screen (it can
be behind other windows; the CLI raises it before each capture and tap).

**4. Grant the helper app three permissions.** Only you can do this. In System Settings >
Privacy & Security:

- **Accessibility** > [+] > press Cmd-Shift-G > paste `~/Applications/FoundryPhone.app` >
  Open > switch it on.
- **Screen Recording** (called "Screen & System Audio Recording" on newer macOS) > [+] >
  same path > switch it on.

- **Automation**: the first `iphone-mirror doctor` run shows a prompt that the helper app
  "wants to control System Events" (that is how it reads the Mirroring window's position).
  Click **Allow**. If you missed it, find the helper app under Automation and switch on
  System Events. Unanswered, the doctor reports a System Events timeout after 8 seconds.

Grants take effect immediately. No restart.

**5. Run the doctor until it is clean.**

```bash
iphone-mirror doctor
```

Expected ending: `=== 9 ok, 0 fail, 0 warn ===`. Each `[FAIL]` line names its fix.

### Why a helper app?

macOS attaches Accessibility, Screen Recording and Automation grants to the *responsible process*.
Grant your terminal and only that terminal works; a headless agent process may have no
way to answer the prompt at all. The client launches the helper app through
LaunchServices once per action, so the helper is always its own responsible process
and carries its own grant, whoever calls it: a terminal, VS Code, Claude Code running
headless, or the MCP server.

The helper lives outside the plugin on purpose. The plugin directory changes on every
plugin update, and a moved bundle loses its grant.

### Security model

- The worker script is copied into the bundle and covered by the code signature.
  `doctor` runs `codesign --verify --deep --strict` on the helper and fails if anything
  edited the bundle since you built it.
- Every rebuild re-signs the app, so macOS treats it as new and asks you to approve
  the grants again. That is by design: the code holding the grant is code you rebuilt.
- Inside the bundle the worker ignores all `IPHONE_MIRROR_*` test hooks, and it parses
  its geometry cache as integers instead of sourcing it, so environment variables and
  files in the state folder cannot change what the granted app runs.
- Limit: macOS does not re-check the bundle's resources on every launch, so a process
  running as you could still edit the bundle itself. `doctor` catches that through the
  signature check; run it at the start of every session (the skill and agent do).
- To remove everything: delete the helper app, remove it from the Privacy lists
  (`tccutil reset All local.foundry.iphone-mirror` does all three for the default bundle ID), and
  delete `$HOME/Library/Caches/foundry-iphone-mirror` and
  `$HOME/Library/Application Support/foundry-iphone-mirror`.

## How to use it

### The loop: screenshot, read, act, verify

```bash
iphone-mirror shot /tmp/iphone-shots/01.png    # prints: path WxHpx window WxHpt
# Read the PNG, pick a target by its pixel position (top-left origin)
iphone-mirror tap 326 700                      # pixels from THAT screenshot
iphone-mirror shot /tmp/iphone-shots/02.png    # verify the screen changed
```

The client converts screenshot pixels to screen points using the geometry recorded by
the last `shot` (Retina 2x handled). Never send two actions without a screenshot
between them: iOS animates and scrolls, so stale coordinates miss. `iphone-mirror map
<px> <py>` prints where a tap would land without touching the phone.

### From Claude Code

- **Ask in plain words** ("open Settings on my iPhone and turn on Dark Mode"). The
  `iphone-mirror` skill loads on its trigger phrases and runs the loop.
- **Delegate long tasks** to the subagent: "Use the iphone-driver agent to walk
  through sign-up in my TestFlight build and screenshot each step." You get back an
  outcome, a step list and evidence paths, not 40 screenshots.
- **MCP tools** are available as `mcp__plugin_foundry-iphone-mirror_iphone__iphone_screenshot`,
  `..._iphone_tap`, `..._iphone_swipe`, `..._iphone_type`, `..._iphone_key`,
  `..._iphone_home`, `..._iphone_doctor`, `..._iphone_open`, `..._iphone_info`,
  `..._iphone_tapxy`. The screenshot comes back inline as an image.

### Real-device QA example

Write acceptance checks first, then run one loop per check and keep a screenshot as
evidence:

```text
Use the iphone-driver agent. App: <your-app> (installed from TestFlight).
Checks:
1. Launch shows the welcome screen with a "Get started" button.
2. Sign up with test account test-user-01 reaches the Home tab.
3. Home tab shows "Hi, test-user-01".
Save one screenshot per check as /tmp/iphone-shots/qa-<n>.png and report pass/fail per check.
```

## Limits

- **iPhone Mirroring must be open, connected and showing the phone.** If the phone is
  unlocked and in use, Mirroring shows "iPhone in Use" and cannot drive it: lock the
  phone. If the session drops, a human may need to approve on the device again.
- **Coordinate taps from screenshots, not element selectors.** There is no
  accessibility tree of the iOS app. Accuracy depends on the model reading the
  screenshot; small or crowded targets can miss, which is why every action is verified.
- **One phone, one action at a time.** Mirroring connects one iPhone to one Mac. The
  client holds a lock, so parallel callers queue.
- **The Mac session must be logged in and unlocked.** A Mac with no display attached
  may capture nothing; use a display or a dummy HDMI plug.
- **Some phone features do not mirror.** The camera, and some protected or
  DRM screens, appear blank or are blocked. Face ID prompts must be answered on the
  phone.
- **Gestures are basic.** Tap, drag-swipe and the home swipe. No multi-touch (pinch,
  rotate), no long-press primitive, no hardware buttons.
- **Typing sends literal keystrokes** that show on the mirror. Do not type secrets.
- **Rebuilding the helper app resets its grants.** After a plugin update, `doctor`
  warns if your helper was built from an older worker; rebuild and re-approve when
  convenient.

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Fix |
|---|---|
| `helper app missing` | `iphone-mirror build` |
| `is not running` | `iphone-mirror open`, then approve on the phone |
| `has no window` | the Mirroring window is closed or minimized; bring it back on screen |
| `window geometry unreadable` / Accessibility FAIL | add the helper app (not your terminal) under Accessibility |
| `System Events did not answer in 8s` | allow the helper app to control System Events (the prompt, or Privacy & Security > Automation) |
| `screenshot empty` / Screen Recording FAIL | add the helper app under Screen Recording |
| `cliclick not found` | `brew install cliclick`, then `iphone-mirror build` and re-approve |
| `no screenshot recorded since the last geometry read` | run `shot` before `tap` or `swipe` (`info` resets the mapping) |
| taps land in the wrong spot | the window moved or resized: take a fresh `shot` |
| LaunchServices error -10669 | the bundle is damaged: `iphone-mirror build` |
| `worker timeout` | the helper did not finish in 30s; check `doctor`, or raise `IPHONE_MIRROR_TIMEOUT` |

## Files

```
foundry-iphone-mirror/
  .claude-plugin/plugin.json
  .mcp.json                     registers the "iphone" MCP server via ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}
  bin/iphone-mirror             the CLI (added to PATH while the plugin is enabled)
  engine/worker.sh              privileged worker, copied into the helper app
  engine/launcher.c             helper app main executable (execs worker.sh)
  engine/build-helper-app.sh    build + sign + register the helper app
  mcp/server.py                 stdlib MCP server over the CLI
  skills/iphone-mirror/SKILL.md the loop and rules
  agents/iphone-driver.md       the delegation subagent
  tests/                        unit tests (no phone needed)
```

State lives in `$HOME/Library/Caches/foundry-iphone-mirror` (geometry cache, IPC
files, default screenshots).

## Tests

No phone, window or permission is needed: geometry is faked and `cliclick` is replaced
by a recorder. Inside the test files, the worker is run directly instead of through the
helper app.

```bash
cd <plugin-dir> && python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v
```

Covers pixel-to-point math (including Retina 2x and bounds), worker guards, the
geom-cache injection guard, test hooks being ignored inside a bundle, client argument
validation and locking, the launcher (compiled with clang, skipped without it), and the
MCP protocol (initialize, tools/list, tools/call, inline PNG, errors).

## Changes from the source

Ported from our production plugin. What changed and why:

- Absolute paths, a personal helper app name and a personal bundle ID were replaced by
  `$HOME` defaults plus `--app`, `--bundle-id` and `--name` build options.
- State moved from a shared `/tmp` folder to a per-user `~/Library/Caches` folder.
- The worker now parses its geometry cache instead of `source`-ing it, ignores test
  hooks inside the bundle, validates coordinates and bounds, and no longer echoes typed
  text back. A helper-function bug that could swallow error messages was fixed.
- The client adds a lock (one action at a time), a `map` dry-run, and a `build` command.
  `doctor` adds macOS version, signature and version-drift checks.
- `cliclick`'s location is recorded at build time, since apps launched by LaunchServices
  get a minimal PATH.
- The MCP server was rewritten on the standard library (no `mcp` package needed).
- The System Events call that reads the window is now bounded (8 seconds), and the
  Automation grant it needs is documented. The source relied on a one-time prompt that
  could leave a fresh install hanging with no explanation.

## License

MIT. Part of the [AI Foundry marketplace](https://github.com/ai-foundry-byu/foundry-marketplace).

plugins.description: Measure agents and prompts: scaffold an eval suite with oracles, code graders, a binary judge and negative controls, run and compare it, and hill-climb one change at a time. Ships evalkit.py (stdlib only).
plugins.readme:
# foundry-evals

Measure agents and prompts. Build an eval suite that can actually fail, run it, compare
with the last run without fooling yourself, and improve a prompt one change at a time.

Ships three skills, one auditing agent, and `evalkit.py`: a single-file, standard-library-only
Python runner you can also copy into any repo for CI.

## Install

Add the marketplace (once):

```text
/plugin marketplace add ai-foundry-byu/foundry-marketplace
```

Install the plugin:

```text
/plugin install foundry-evals@ai-foundry
```

Or from a shell:

```bash
claude plugin install foundry-evals@ai-foundry
```

## What is in it

| item | type | what it does | SDLC stage | maturity |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `new-eval` | skill | scaffold a suite: cases, target runner, code graders first, a binary judge only where code cannot grade, do-nothing and pushover controls, a threshold | test design | method proven; tooling new |
| `run-eval` | skill | run, read the report in the right order, compare with the last run, report only measured numbers | test / verify | method proven; tooling new |
| `hillclimb` | skill | one change per round, keep only changes above the noise band, train/val/test discipline, cost staircase | improve / optimize | method proven; tooling new |
| `eval-auditor` | agent | audits a suite for ambiguous cases, cheatable or over-strict graders, missing hold cases, bad judge rubrics, saturated or noisy runs | review | new |
| `scripts/evalkit.py` (also `bin/evalkit`) | script | the runner: init, run, check, compare, history | test / CI gate | new (standalone port) |
| `scripts/judge_claude.py` | script | binary LLM judge through `claude -p`: critique, then a single VERDICT line | test | new |
| `templates/example-suite` | template | `refund-triage`, a 9-case suite with an offline target, a model target, controls and a deliberate bug to find | learning | new |

**Maturity, honestly.** "Proven" here means the METHOD (code graders first, binary judges,
negative controls, errors never scored as zeros, pass^k, same cases or no comparison, one
change per climb round, train/val/test splits) is how the AI Foundry team's own eval
framework works in production today. `evalkit.py`, the judge script, the agent and the
templates are NEW: a standalone port written for this marketplace, covered by unit tests but
not yet battle-tested by other teams. Report bugs as issues.

## Quickstart (2 minutes, no API key)

```bash
evalkit init evals/refund-triage
cd evals/refund-triage
evalkit check . --no-judge
evalkit run . --no-judge --gate
```

If `evalkit` is not on PATH (the plugin's `bin/` is added only while the plugin is enabled),
use `python3 "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/evalkit.py"` inside Claude Code, or copy
`scripts/evalkit.py` into your repo and run `python3 evalkit.py`.

The first run scores 77.8% and fails the 90% gate: two final-sale cases sit at 0% because the
example target has a deliberate bug. Ask Claude "use the hillclimb skill on this suite" to
find and fix it, then rerun and read the comparison.

## How to use each item

**new-eval.** Say "add an eval for my summarizer" or "build evals for this agent". The skill
walks through: define good, scaffold with `evalkit init`, wire your target (JSON in on stdin,
one JSON object out on stdout), write cases with oracles, choose graders, add a judge only for
fuzzy criteria, add controls, set the threshold, and pass `evalkit check`.

**run-eval.** Say "run the evals" or "did my change help". It runs a pilot, the full run with
reps, reads the report (warnings, 0% cases, failures, flips, then numbers), and reads the
comparison (NOT COMPARABLE, within noise, improved, regressed).

**hillclimb.** Say "improve this prompt against the eval" or "make it cheaper without losing
quality". One change per round, keep or revert on val, confirm on test, log every round.

**eval-auditor.** Say "audit my eval suite at evals/x". It runs the free `evalkit check`,
reads every case and the latest run, and reports findings with evidence and fixes. It does not
edit files and does not run paid model calls unless you ask.

## evalkit reference

```bash
evalkit init <dir>                       # copy the example suite (plus judge.py)
evalkit check <suite> [--no-judge]       # oracles pass, empty output fails, controls score low
evalkit run <suite> [--reps N] [--split train|val|test|all] [--cases a,b] [--tag t]
                    [--label L] [--no-judge] [--target CMD] [--out .evals]
                    [--gate | --fail-under X] [--fail-metric score|pass_hat_k]
evalkit compare <suite> | <a.json> <b.json>
evalkit history <suite>
```

Target protocol: stdin `{"case_id", "rep", "input"}`; stdout one JSON object; optional
`"_meta": {"cost_usd": n}`. Non-zero exit, timeout or non-JSON output is an error trial, kept
out of the score and listed in the report.

Graders: `exact`, `contains`, `regex`, `json_field` (`equals`, `one_of`, `exists`, `is`),
`judge`. All take `path` (dotted) and `negate`.

Judge protocol: stdin `{"case_id", "input", "expected", "output", "criterion", "rubric"}`;
stdout `{"pass": true|false|null, "reason": "..."}`. `null` (UNKNOWN) is an error, not a pass.

Outputs: `.evals/<suite>/<run_id>.json` (every trial and grader verdict, fingerprints of the
case set, graders, target command and surfaces) and `.evals/<suite>/<run_id>.md` (summary,
comparison, failures, errors).

Exit codes: 0 ok, 2 config error, 3 no scorable trial, 4 below gate, 5 check failed.

CI example (GitHub Actions step):

```yaml
- run: python3 tools/evalkit.py run evals/refund-triage --gate --quiet
```

## Requirements

- Python 3.9 or newer. No packages.
- Claude Code CLI on PATH only for `judge_claude.py` and the example `target_claude.py`
  (both call `claude -p --output-format json`). Set `EVALKIT_JUDGE_MODEL` and
  `EVALKIT_TARGET_MODEL` to pin models, `EVALKIT_CLAUDE_BIN` to use another binary.

## Tests

```bash
cd "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}"
python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts/tests -v
```

24 offline tests: every grader, pass@k and pass^k math, error handling (crash, junk stdout,
timeout), judge wiring and cost sums, the example suite end to end (baseline fails the gate,
the one-line fix passes, comparison names the two fixed cases), case-set change detection,
control and empty-output self-tests, CLI exit codes.

## Known limitations

- Trials run one at a time. Large suites against slow models take a while; that is deliberate.
- `claude -p` targets and judges inherit your Claude Code settings, plugins and project
  instructions from the directory they run in. For a clean measurement, run the suite from a
  directory without a project CLAUDE.md, or use your own API-based target.
- No automated hill-climber: the `hillclimb` skill drives the loop by hand with evalkit.
- No multi-turn conversation or tool-sandbox harness. For a full agent environment (mock
  store, tool-call graders, judge validation with human labels), see
  [agent-evals-starter](https://github.com/jddavenportOpen/agent-evals-starter) (MIT), which
  this plugin's control and grader ideas are adapted from.
- Bootstrap intervals over a few dozen cases are wide and somewhat optimistic (reps of one
  case are not independent). Treat small deltas as noise.

## License

MIT. Part of the [AI Foundry marketplace](https://github.com/ai-foundry-byu/foundry-marketplace).
