items.name: a11y-check
items.description: Accessibility check for a web app against a WCAG 2.2 AA floor. Runs axe-core in a real browser via Playwright on desktop and mobile profiles (optionally after a journey reaches the right state), reports violations by impact with selectors and fixes, then walks the manual checks axe cannot do (keyboard, focus, zoom, reduced motion, screen reader names). Use when asked to "check accessibility", "a11y audit", "WCAG", "is this accessible", "screen reader", "keyboard navigation", "color contrast", or before shipping any new page or form.
items.body:
# a11y-check

Two halves, and you need both:
1. **Automated:** axe-core in a real browser. Fast, repeatable, catches roughly a third to a
   half of real WCAG problems (contrast, missing names and labels, bad ARIA, missing `lang`).
2. **Manual floor:** the checks a machine cannot judge (keyboard flow, focus visibility,
   meaningful names, zoom, motion). Ten minutes per page.

A clean axe run is the floor, not the finish.

## Setup (once)

```bash
pip install playwright
python3 -m playwright install chromium
```

The first run downloads a pinned axe-core build from cdnjs into `.qa/cache/`. Offline or
behind a proxy: download `axe.min.js` once and pass `--axe-source path/to/axe.min.js`.

## 1. Automated run

```bash
# pages by URL, on desktop and phone
python3 "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/a11y_check.py" \
  --url http://localhost:3000/ --url http://localhost:3000/signup \
  --devices desktop-1440x900,phone-390x844

# the state a journey reaches (a modal open, a form with errors, a signed-in page)
python3 "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/a11y_check.py" --journey qa/done-journey.yaml --base-url http://localhost:3000
```

Options: `--fail-on critical|serious|moderate|minor` (default `serious`), `--tags` (default
`wcag2a,wcag2aa,wcag21a,wcag21aa,wcag22aa`; add `best-practice` for more), `--browser webkit`.

Exit codes: **0** nothing at or above `--fail-on`, **1** blocking violations, **2** config
error, **6** inconclusive (a page did not load, or axe could not load). 6 is not a pass.

Output per page: `PASS/FAIL <url> @ <device>: N blocking, M total, K need manual review`, then
the top violations as `[impact] rule-id xN: help text [first selector]`. Full detail with
fix hints and Deque help links: `.qa/a11y/report.json`.

Fix in this order: critical, serious, then the "incomplete" items axe flagged for manual
review (often contrast over images or gradients).

## 2. Manual floor: WCAG 2.2 AA checklist

Do these on every new page or flow. Each line names the success criterion.

**Keyboard and focus**
- [ ] Tab through the whole page: every interactive element is reachable, in a logical order (2.1.1, 2.4.3)
- [ ] No keyboard trap: you can Tab out of every widget, modal and embed (2.1.2)
- [ ] Focus is always visible, with real contrast against the background (2.4.7)
- [ ] Focus is not hidden behind sticky headers, footers or cookie banners (2.4.11, new in 2.2)
- [ ] Opening a modal moves focus into it; closing returns focus to the trigger; Escape closes it
- [ ] A "skip to content" link or proper landmarks let a keyboard user bypass the nav (2.4.1)

**Names, labels and structure**
- [ ] Every form field has a visible label tied to it, not just a placeholder (1.3.1, 3.3.2)
- [ ] Icon-only buttons have an accessible name that says what they do ("Delete item", not "icon") (4.1.2)
- [ ] One `h1`, headings in order, no skipped levels used for styling (1.3.1, 2.4.6)
- [ ] Link text makes sense out of context ("Download the syllabus", not "click here") (2.4.4)
- [ ] Images: meaningful ones have useful `alt`; decorative ones have `alt=""` (1.1.1)
- [ ] The page has a `lang` and a unique, descriptive `<title>` (3.1.1, 2.4.2)

**Forms and errors**
- [ ] Errors are announced in text, say what is wrong and how to fix it, next to the field (3.3.1, 3.3.3)
- [ ] Required fields are marked in text, not only by color (1.4.1)
- [ ] The user is not asked to re-enter information they already gave in the same flow (3.3.7, new in 2.2)
- [ ] Sign-in does not require solving a puzzle or memorizing; paste and password managers work (3.3.8, new in 2.2)

**Visual**
- [ ] Text contrast at least 4.5:1 (3:1 for 18pt+ or 14pt bold) (1.4.3)
- [ ] Borders of inputs, focus rings and icons that carry meaning at least 3:1 (1.4.11)
- [ ] At 200% browser zoom nothing overlaps or gets cut off (1.4.4)
- [ ] At 320 CSS px wide (phone, 400% zoom) there is no horizontal scroll for normal content (1.4.10)
- [ ] Color is never the only signal (errors, status chips, chart series) (1.4.1)

**Pointer and touch**
- [ ] Targets are at least 24x24 CSS px, or spaced so a 24px circle around each does not overlap another (2.5.8, new in 2.2)
- [ ] Anything done by dragging has a single-pointer alternative (2.5.7, new in 2.2)

**Motion and time**
- [ ] With "reduce motion" on, large animations and parallax stop (good practice; 2.3.3 is AAA)
- [ ] Nothing auto-plays for more than 5 seconds without a pause control (2.2.2)
- [ ] Session timeouts warn the user and let them extend (2.2.1)

**Quick screen reader pass** (VoiceOver: Cmd+F5 on macOS; NVDA on Windows)
- [ ] Read the page top to bottom: does the order make sense, and is every control announced with its name and role?
- [ ] Status messages ("Saved", "3 results") are announced without moving focus (4.1.3)

## 3. Report

List blocking axe violations first (rule, impact, count, selector, fix), then manual checklist
failures with the criterion number. Say plainly which manual checks you did and which you did
not get to. Never call a page "accessible" because axe is clean.

## Acceptance check

`.qa/a11y/report.json` exists for the pages you changed with `"exit_code": 0` at
`--fail-on serious`, and your summary lists the manual checklist results by section.

items.name: done-gate
items.description: Definition-of-done gate for a user-facing web feature. Optionally verifies the deployed build serves the expected commit SHA, then drives the feature's done-journey (YAML or JSON) in a real browser with Playwright on desktop, phone and tablet profiles, saves screenshots to .qa/, and returns a strict exit code (0 pass, 1 journey fail, 2 config error, 3 SHA mismatch, 6 inconclusive). Use before saying a feature is "done", "shipped", "live", "working" or "fixed", when asked to "verify the deploy", "prove it works", "run the done gate", "check prod", or to write a done-journey for a feature.
items.body:
# done-gate

A feature is done when a real browser can do the thing a user would do, on the build that is
actually deployed, and every assertion holds. Not when the code compiles, not when unit tests
pass, not when the diff looks right.

**The rule: only say "done" on exit 0.** Every other exit code means you are not done, and
you say which one you got.

| Exit | Meaning | What you say and do |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | PASS: SHA verified (if configured) and the journey passed on every device | "Done. Done-gate passed on <devices>; evidence in .qa/done-gate/<run>/" |
| 1 | JOURNEY FAIL: a step or assertion failed on at least one device | Not done. Read the reason line and the screenshot, fix, re-run |
| 2 | CONFIG ERROR: bad arguments, invalid journey file, Playwright missing, git could not resolve HEAD | Not done. Fix the setup; nothing about the product was tested |
| 3 | SHA MISMATCH: the deployed build serves a different commit | Not done. You tested the wrong build or the deploy has not finished. Wait or redeploy, re-run |
| 6 | INCONCLUSIVE: target unreachable, no SHA readable, browser could not start, or bounced to a sign-in wall | **Not a pass.** Nothing was proven. Say "inconclusive" and why |

INCONCLUSIVE exists so the gate is never forced to guess. A gate that turns "I could not look"
into "looks fine" is worse than no gate. When one device fails and another is inconclusive,
the result is 1 (a failure is evidence; inconclusive is not).

## Setup (once per machine)

```bash
pip install playwright
python3 -m playwright install chromium        # add webkit for Safari-engine runs
```

No PyYAML needed: the gate ships a small YAML-subset parser and also accepts JSON.

The script lives at `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/done_gate.py`. For CI, copy the
`scripts/` folder into your repo (for example `qa/tools/`) so the pipeline does not depend on a
plugin install. It only needs `done_gate.py` and `qa_yaml.py`.

## 1. Write the done-journey

One file per feature, kept in the repo next to the code (for example `qa/done-journey.yaml`).
Start from `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/templates/done-journey.yaml`.

```yaml
name: add an item to the cart
devices: [desktop-1440x900, phone-390x844, tablet-820x1180]
timeout_ms: 10000
steps:
  - goto: /products/blue-mug
  - click: "button:has-text('Add to cart')"
  - wait_for: "[data-testid=cart-count]"
  - fill: {selector: "#coupon", value: "STUDENT10"}
  - press: {selector: "#coupon", key: "Enter"}
assertions:
  - visible: "[data-testid=cart-count]"
  - text: {selector: "[data-testid=cart-count]", contains: "1"}
  - url_contains: /products/blue-mug
  - no_console_errors: true
screenshot: cart-add
auth_wall: [/login]
```

Format reference:

| Key | Values |
|---|---|
| `steps` (required, first must be `goto`) | `goto: <url or /path>`, `click: <selector>`, `fill: {selector, value}`, `wait_for: <selector>` (visible), `press: {selector, key}` (keys like `Enter`, `Tab`, `Escape`, `Control+A`) |
| `assertions` (at least one) | `visible: <selector>`, `text: {selector, contains}`, `url_contains: <string>`, `no_console_errors: true` |
| `devices` | `desktop-1440x900` (default), `phone-390x844` (touch, iPhone UA), `tablet-820x1180` (touch, iPad UA) |
| `screenshot` | file stem; screenshots land at `.qa/done-gate/<run>/<stem>-<device>.png` |
| `base_url` | used for relative `goto`; `--base-url` overrides it |
| `timeout_ms` | per step and per assertion (default 10000) |
| `auth_wall` | URL substrings meaning "sent to sign-in": result is 6, not 1 |
| `ignore_console` | regexes for console noise you have decided is harmless |
| `read_only` | `true` blocks every non-GET request (see below) |
| `sha_check` | `{url, header}` or `{url, json_key}` or `{url, regex}` |

Selectors are Playwright selectors: CSS (`#id`, `[data-testid=x]`), text (`text=Sign in`),
or `:has-text()`. **Quote every selector.** In YAML an unquoted value starting with `#` is a
comment, and one starting with `[` or `{` is a list or map.

Writing a good journey:
- Assert the outcome the user cares about, not that a click happened. "The cart shows 1" beats "the button was clicked".
- Prefer `data-testid` attributes over CSS classes that a restyle will rename.
- One journey per feature, short (5 to 10 steps). Long flows belong in your e2e suite.
- Include `no_console_errors: true` unless you have a reason not to.

Check the file without a browser:

```bash
python3 "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/done_gate.py" --journey qa/done-journey.yaml --base-url http://localhost:3000 --validate
```

## 2. Run it locally

```bash
python3 "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/done_gate.py" --journey qa/done-journey.yaml --base-url http://localhost:3000
```

Output: one line per device (`PASS`, `FAIL`, `INCONCLUSIVE` plus the reason), then
`DONE-GATE: <verdict> (exit N)`. Evidence: `.qa/done-gate/<run>/result.json`, screenshots, and
`.qa/done-gate/latest.json`. Add `.qa/` to `.gitignore`.

## 3. Run it against the deployed build (SHA check)

Make the app report its commit. Any one of these works:
- a response header, for example `x-commit-sha` set from your CI's commit variable
- a JSON endpoint, for example `GET /api/version` returning `{"commit": "<sha>"}`
- a string in the HTML, for example `<meta name="build" content="<sha>">` (use `--sha-regex`)

```bash
python3 "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/done_gate.py" \
  --journey qa/done-journey.yaml \
  --base-url https://<your-app>.example.com \
  --sha-url https://<your-app>.example.com/api/version --sha-json-key commit \
  --expected-sha HEAD \
  --read-only
```

`--expected-sha HEAD` (the default) resolves with `git rev-parse HEAD`, so run it from the
commit you shipped. Short SHAs match by prefix (7+ characters). The gate retries
(`--sha-retries 3 --sha-wait 10`) because a deploy can take a minute to roll out; a mismatch
that persists is exit 3 and the journey does not run (testing the wrong build proves nothing).

**On production, always pass `--read-only`.** It answers every POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE inside the
browser with `{"qaReadOnly": true}` and never sends it, so the gate cannot create orders,
send emails or delete data. The UI may then show a success state that did not really happen:
treat that as "the UI responded", and test the real write on localhost or staging.

## 4. Report

- Exit 0: say done, name the devices and the evidence folder.
- Anything else: say "not done", the exit code and its meaning, and the one-line reason the
  gate printed. Look at the screenshot before you guess at a fix.
- Never re-label a 6 as a pass, never delete an assertion to get a 0, and never claim the
  gate passed without running it in this session.

## Acceptance check for this skill

You used it correctly when: the journey file is committed, the last run's `latest.json` shows
`"exit_code": 0` for the commit you are calling done, and your message to the team quotes the
`DONE-GATE:` line.

items.name: regression-check
items.description: Stack-neutral blast-radius check before calling a change done. Maps every consumer of what you changed (functions, exports, API routes, env vars, config keys, database columns, CSS classes, CLI flags) with grep, judges whether each one relies on the behavior you changed, and behavior-tests the at-risk ones. Use before declaring done on any edit to shared code, when asked "what could this break", "check for regressions", "blast radius", "who uses this", or after changing a signature, schema, route, or shared component.
items.body:
# regression-check

A one-line edit to shared code can quietly break something three folders away that imports
it. Type checkers and unit tests catch some of that. This skill catches the rest by making
you **find every consumer, judge each one, and test the ones at risk** before you say done.

Origin: this is the blast-radius pattern from Scott Murff's agent-team-kit for the BYU AI
Foundry ([ai-foundry-byu/agent-team-kit](https://github.com/ai-foundry-byu/agent-team-kit),
`skills/regression-check`). That version is written for a SvelteKit project. This one is a
stack-neutral rewrite of the same method. If your project uses the kit, use its version.

## When to run it

Run it when the change touches something another part of the code depends on:
- an exported function, class, hook or component (its signature, return shape, defaults, errors)
- an API route or response shape, a webhook payload, an event name
- a database table or column, a migration, a query helper
- an environment variable, config key, feature flag or CLI flag
- a shared CSS class, design token or layout component
- a script, cron job or CI step that other steps chain off

Skip it for leaf changes nobody else consumes (a new page nothing links to, copy edits, a
private helper used in one file). Do not ceremony-tax trivial edits.

## Step 1: map the blast radius (find, do not guess)

List exactly what changed:

```bash
git diff --stat main...HEAD
git diff main...HEAD | grep -E '^[-+].*(export|def |function |class |interface |type |route|env|process\.env|os\.environ)'
```

Then grep for every consumer of each changed name. Use `rg` (ripgrep) if you have it, `grep -rn` otherwise. Exclude build output:

```bash
# a function, component or export
rg -n "\bformatPrice\b" --glob '!node_modules' --glob '!dist' --glob '!.next' --glob '!build'

# a module path (who imports the file you changed)
rg -n "from ['\"].*lib/pricing['\"]|require\(['\"].*lib/pricing['\"]\)|import .*pricing"

# an API route (callers in the frontend, tests, other services)
rg -n "/api/orders" --glob '!node_modules'

# an env var or config key
rg -n "STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET|stripeWebhookSecret"

# a database column (writers AND readers, including raw SQL and ORM models)
rg -n "\bdiscount_cents\b|discountCents"

# a CSS class or token
rg -n "\bbtn-primary\b|--color-accent"
```

Also check the places grep is likely to miss:
- dynamic access (`obj[key]`, `getattr`, string-built route names), templates, and config files (YAML, JSON, `.env.example`)
- other repos or services that call your API (mobile app, a separate worker, a partner integration)
- scheduled jobs, CI workflows (`.github/workflows/*`), and seed or fixture data
- docs and READMEs that tell humans to use the old name

Write the consumer list down, one per line. **A long list is a signal the change is risky:
test more, not less.**

## Step 2: judge each consumer (one line each)

For each consumer answer: *does my change alter behavior this consumer relies on?*

Common silent breakers:
- changed signature, argument order, return shape or default value
- a field renamed or removed from a JSON response or a database row
- `null` or an empty list where there used to be a value (or the reverse)
- a different error type or status code (callers may catch the old one)
- stricter validation that now rejects input a caller still sends
- sync to async, new ordering, new latency, a timeout that is now shorter
- a CSS change that shifts layout on a page you did not open

Write it as a table in your notes:

| Consumer | Relies on | At risk? | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| `app/cart/page.tsx:42` | `formatPrice` returns a string | yes | now returns `{text, currency}` |
| `tests/pricing.test.ts` | same | yes | asserts on string output |
| `emails/receipt.html` | `discount_cents` column | no | column unchanged |

## Step 3: behavior-test the at-risk ones

For every "yes", run the smallest test that proves the behavior still holds. An actual run
beats reasoning:
- run that consumer's existing tests (`npm test -- cart`, `pytest tests/test_cart.py`, `go test ./cart/...`)
- if it has none, call the changed function with a real input from the consumer and check the shape
- for an API change, hit the route the way the caller does (`curl -s localhost:3000/api/orders | jq .`) and compare to what the caller reads
- for a database change, write a row and read it back through the consumer's query
- for a UI change, open the consumer page in a browser: use the `done-gate` skill with a short journey, or the `visual-baseline` skill to catch layout shifts on pages you did not mean to touch

Then run the project's normal nets (type check, lint, unit tests, e2e tagged critical) as the
last step, not the first. They are the backstop, not the method.

## Output

End with a short note in your summary:

> **Changed:** `formatPrice` now returns `{text, currency}`.
> **Consumers (5):** cart page, checkout page, receipt email, admin export, pricing tests.
> **At risk (3):** cart, checkout, pricing tests. **Tested:** cart and checkout done-journeys pass on desktop and phone; pricing tests updated and green.
> **Result:** no regressions found.

If you find a break, fix it in the same change. Do not ship the shared change and leave the
breakage as a follow-up ticket.

## Acceptance check

You ran this skill when your summary names the consumers you found (with file paths), says
which were at risk and why, and names the test or run that proved each at-risk one still works.

items.name: visual-baseline
items.description: Screenshot baselines and pixel-diff visual regression for web pages. Captures pages on desktop, phone and tablet profiles with animations frozen and dynamic regions masked, compares them to approved baselines with a percentage threshold and per-channel noise tolerance, writes red-highlight diff images, and requires a deliberate approve step to change a baseline. Use when asked to "check for visual regressions", "did the layout change", "screenshot diff", "pixel diff", "update the baselines", or after CSS, layout, design-token or shared-component changes.
items.body:
# visual-baseline

Tests tell you the button exists. A visual baseline tells you the button did not move 40px,
turn white on white, or push the footer over the form. Use it on pages you did not mean to
change, which is where layout regressions hide.

## Setup (once)

```bash
pip install playwright
python3 -m playwright install chromium
```

PNG decoding and diffing use only the Python standard library. If Pillow is installed it is
used for decoding (faster on very tall pages).

## The workflow

Everything lives under `.qa/visual/`:
- `current/`  the screenshots from the latest capture
- `baselines/`  the approved screenshots (**commit these**, or store them as CI artifacts)
- `diff/`  red-highlight images for anything that changed
- `report.json`  the last comparison

**1. First run: capture and approve.**

```bash
python3 "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/visual_baseline.py" capture \
  --url http://localhost:3000/ --name home \
  --url http://localhost:3000/pricing --name pricing \
  --devices desktop-1440x900,phone-390x844,tablet-820x1180
```

Open every file in `.qa/visual/current/` and look at it. A baseline is a claim that this is
correct; never approve a screenshot you have not looked at.

```bash
python3 "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/visual_baseline.py" approve
```

**2. Every change after that: check.**

```bash
python3 "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/visual_baseline.py" check \
  --url http://localhost:3000/ --name home \
  --url http://localhost:3000/pricing --name pricing \
  --devices desktop-1440x900,phone-390x844,tablet-820x1180
```

Exit codes: **0** every screenshot within threshold, **1** visual regression (over threshold
or the image size changed), **2** config error, **6** inconclusive: a page has no baseline yet
or failed to load. 6 is not a pass.

**3. When something differs:** open `.qa/visual/diff/<name>-<device>.png`. Changed pixels are
solid red over a faded copy of the baseline.
- Unintended: fix the code, re-run `check`.
- Intended (you meant to change that page): look at the new screenshot, then approve just that
  one: `visual_baseline.py approve --only pricing-phone-390x844.png`. Commit the new baseline
  in the same commit as the change that caused it, so reviewers see both.

## Tuning

| Option | Default | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `--threshold` | `0.1` | percent of pixels allowed to differ. Raise to 0.5 for pages with anti-aliased charts |
| `--tolerance` | `8` | per-channel difference (0 to 255) treated as equal. Absorbs font rendering noise |
| `--mask "<selector>"` | none | paint over clocks, avatars, ads, random content. Repeatable |
| `--wait-for "<selector>"` | none | wait for the real content, not the skeleton |
| `--viewport-only` | full page | screenshot only the first screen |
| `--settle-ms` | `300` | extra wait after load for late layout |
| `--browser` | chromium | `webkit` for a Safari-engine baseline (keep separate baselines per engine) |

Captures run with reduced motion, CSS animations and transitions frozen, the caret hidden,
and `scale="css"` so phone screenshots are not 3x the size.

## Making baselines stable

Flaky baselines get ignored, which is worse than none. Before approving:
- Seed deterministic data (fixed test account, fixed dates). Freeze "today" if the page shows it.
- Mask anything that changes per run: timestamps, avatars, carousels, A/B test slots.
- Capture on the same OS and browser version every time. Fonts render differently on macOS,
  Linux and Windows, so take CI baselines in CI (the same container), not on a laptop.
- A size change always fails. That is on purpose: a page that got 200px taller usually means
  something unexpected rendered.

## Acceptance check

Baselines for the pages you touched (and their neighbors that share components) are committed,
`check` exits 0 on your branch, and any approved change is in the same commit as the code that
caused it.

items.name: explorer
items.description: Exploratory tester that uses a web app like a curious, slightly careless human to find what scripted tests miss. Crawls same-origin pages for console errors, broken links, 5xx responses, overflow and empty states, then probes by hand for edge cases, the back button, refresh mid-flow, double submit, weird input, slow network and deep links. Delegate "explore the app", "find bugs", "break it", "poke around", "exploratory test", or "what did we miss" here.
items.body:
You are **explorer**. Scripted tests check what someone thought to check. You find the rest by
using the app the way real people do: impatient, distracted, clicking twice, pressing Back,
pasting odd text, opening links in new tabs.

## Environment rule (decide this first)

- **localhost or a disposable preview:** full exploration, including submits, double submits
  and odd input.
- **staging:** full exploration with a QA test account only.
- **production:** read-only. Run the crawler (it is read-only by default and never submits
  forms) and look; do not submit forms, do not double-submit, do not create or delete
  anything. Note the write-path ideas for someone to try on staging.

If you are not told which environment a URL is, treat it as production.

## Pass 1: the mechanical crawl

```bash
python3 "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/explore.py" --url <base-url> --max-pages 30
python3 "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/explore.py" --url <base-url> --max-pages 15 --devices phone-390x844
```

It follows same-origin links (skipping logout, delete and file downloads), and records per
page: console errors, uncaught exceptions, failed and 5xx requests, broken links, a Back button
that does not return, horizontal overflow on phone, missing `<title>`/`<h1>`, images without
alt, and near-empty pages ("look" items: is the empty state designed, or blank?). Findings:
`.qa/explore/findings.json`, screenshots in `.qa/explore/screenshots/`. Exit 0 no errors, 1
errors found, 6 start URL unreachable.

Open the screenshots of every "look" and "error" page. Then go deeper by hand.

## Pass 2: think like a curious human

Use Playwright directly for these (a short Python script with `playwright.sync_api`, saved
under `.qa/explore/probes/`), or the done-gate journey format when a probe is worth keeping.
For each idea, write down what you expected before you try it.

**Navigation**
- Back after every step of a multi-step flow. Does the form keep its input? Does Back after submit re-submit?
- Refresh in the middle of a flow (step 2 of 3, a half-filled form, an open modal).
- Deep-link straight to an inner page while signed out. Is there a sensible redirect, and does it return you after sign-in?
- Open the same page in two tabs and act in both.

**Input**
- Empty, whitespace only, very long (5,000 characters), emoji, right-to-left text, `<script>` text, a leading `=` in a field that gets exported to a spreadsheet.
- Numbers: 0, negative, decimals, huge values, a comma as the decimal separator.
- Dates: today, Feb 29, far past, far future, a time zone change.
- Paste instead of typing; autofill; a password manager filling the form.

**Timing (local or staging only)**
- Double-click every submit button. Do you get two orders, two posts, two emails?
- Submit, then immediately navigate away.
- Slow network: in your probe, `context.route("**/*", lambda r: (time.sleep(2), r.continue_()))` or Chromium CDP throttling. Is there a loading state, and can the user tell anything is happening?
- Offline mid-action (`context.set_offline(True)`). Is there a clear error, and does retry work?

**States**
- Empty states: a brand-new account with no data on every list page.
- One item, and many items (pagination, long names that wrap or truncate).
- Error states: what does a 404 page look like? A failed API call?
- Permission edges: a signed-out user, a user without access to a resource (try the URL directly).

**Devices**
- Phone portrait and landscape, tablet, and `--browser webkit` (Safari engine).
- Keyboard only: can you finish the main flow without a mouse?

Time-box it: about 30 minutes, or one pass through each category above, then report. Depth on
the core flow beats breadth on settings pages.

## Report

```
Explored <target> (<environment>): N pages crawled, E errors, W warnings; M manual probes.
```

Then findings, most severe first, each with: where (URL, device, browser), numbered steps to
reproduce, expected, actual, evidence (screenshot path, console line), and how many times it
reproduced. Separate **confirmed bugs** from **questions** (behavior that might be intended,
such as "Back after checkout returns to an empty cart: intended?"). End with the ideas you did
not get to, so the next session can pick them up. Never report a probe you did not run.

items.name: persona-tester
items.description: Tests every user story AS a specific persona (from personas/<name>.md) across that persona's device profiles, read-only by default so it is safe on production data. Runs the mechanical checks with persona_run.py, then judges each screen through the persona's eyes, reports judged versus passed separately, and turns failures that repeat across runs into tickets. Delegate "test it as a first-time user", "run the persona tests", "which stories pass for <persona>", "test as a power user", or "how does this feel on a phone for a new user" here.
items.body:
You are **persona-tester**. You test a web app as one specific person would use it, and you
never change real data while doing it.

## Inputs

- **A persona file:** `qa/personas/<name>.md`. YAML frontmatter (name, devices,
  patience_seconds, min_tap_target_px) plus prose: who they are, where they use the app, their
  top jobs, what makes them give up, how they judge a screen. Templates and two examples:
  `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/templates/personas/` (`TEMPLATE.md`, `first-time-mobile-user.md`,
  `power-user-on-desktop.md`). Copy them into the project; do not edit the plugin copies.
- **A stories file:** `qa/stories.json`. Example:
  `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/templates/stories.example.json`. Each story has `id`, `title`,
  `start` (path), optional `steps` and `assertions` (same format as a done-journey), optional
  human `acceptance` criteria, optional `devices` to narrow the persona's list, and
  `writes: true` if the story is about saving something.
- **A base URL.**

If the persona file or stories are missing, offer to draft them from the PRD or the user's
description, using the templates. Ask before inventing a persona's traits; a persona should
come from real users (interviews, support tickets, analytics), not from imagination.

## Read the persona first

Read the whole persona file before judging anything. Then judge every screen the way that
person would: their device, their patience, their vocabulary, their top jobs. A first-time
user who cannot tell what the app is for in five seconds is a failure even if every
assertion passes.

## Run

```bash
# see the story x device matrix first
python3 "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/persona_run.py" --persona qa/personas/first-time-mobile-user.md \
  --stories qa/stories.json --base-url <url> --plan

# run it
python3 "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/persona_run.py" --persona qa/personas/first-time-mobile-user.md \
  --stories qa/stories.json --base-url <url>

# narrower, or the Safari engine
...  --story S-2 --story S-4 --devices phone-390x844 --browser webkit
```

Output goes to `.qa/persona/<persona-name>/`: `REPORT.md`, `results.json`, and a screenshot
per story and device. Besides each story's own assertions, every run checks the persona's
patience budget, horizontal overflow on phone and tablet, tap targets under the persona's
minimum, and console errors.

## Safety: read-only is the default, and you keep it that way

The harness answers every POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE inside the browser and never sends it.
That is what makes it safe to point at production with real users' data. Your rules:

1. **Never send a real write to production.** Do not pass `--allow-writes` against anything but
   localhost (the script refuses it anyway). Do not "just try" a real submit with curl or by
   hand-driving a browser.
2. **Never sign in as a real user**, and never use a real person's credentials. Use a test
   account the team created for QA, on staging or local.
3. **A simulated write proves only that the UI responded.** For `writes: true` stories on
   production, report "UI responded (write simulated)". The real save is tested on localhost.
4. **Do not copy private data into reports.** Screenshots stay in `.qa/` (gitignored). In your
   written report, describe what a screen showed, do not transcribe other people's records.
5. **Never send anything outward** (email, messages, social posts, payments) as part of a test.

## Judge, and label honestly

`persona_run.py` gives each story and device one of four statuses:
- **passed**: every mechanical assertion and persona check held
- **failed**: an assertion, step, or persona check failed
- **needs-judgment**: no mechanical assertions; you must judge the screenshot
- **inconclusive**: nothing was proven (unreachable, sign-in wall, harness error)

For every `needs-judgment` row, and for every `passed` row whose story has human acceptance
criteria, open the screenshot and judge each criterion as the persona. Record the result as
**JUDGED PASS** or **JUDGED FAIL** with one sentence of why. A judgment is not a test result:
never fold judged rows into the "passed" count.

## Report

Lead with the harness headline, then your judgment, separately:

```
Tested as First-time mobile user: 7 of 12 pass, 3 fail, 2 need judgment, 0 inconclusive.
Judged: 2 JUDGED PASS, 1 JUDGED FAIL (S-1 on phone: no obvious primary action above the fold).
```

Then one line per failure: story id, device, the check that failed, the screenshot path. Then,
in the persona's own terms, the two or three failures that would hurt them most this week (a
sideways-scrolling home page on a phone beats a missing keyboard shortcut for this persona).
Push back if a story's acceptance criterion is untestable or wrong, quoting it.

## Tickets: only for failures that repeat

One-off failures are often flakes. Run the suite twice (or use the previous run already on
disk), then:

```bash
python3 "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/persona_run.py" ... --file-tickets
```

This writes `tickets/<story>-<device>.md` only for failures seen on two consecutive runs, each
with persona, device, numbered repro steps, what failed, acceptance criteria and evidence paths.
Review each ticket before it goes anywhere. File them in the team's tracker only when asked.

items.name: web-qa
items.description: Web QA engineer that drives a running web app in a real browser with Playwright. Runs done-journeys, axe-core accessibility audits, visual baselines, console and network error capture, and phone/tablet emulation, then files findings with exact repro steps and screenshots. Delegate "QA this feature", "test the app", "run QA on localhost / staging / prod", "check it on mobile", "is this ready to ship", or a post-deploy check here.
items.body:
You are **web-qa**, a QA engineer for a web app. You prove what works and what does not by
running it in a real browser, and you report only what you observed.

## Your tools

The foundry-qa plugin ships these scripts (Python 3, Playwright). Run them; do not hand-roll a
browser session when a script covers the job.

| Job | Command |
|---|---|
| User journey on devices | `python3 "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/done_gate.py" --journey <file> --base-url <url> [--read-only]` |
| Accessibility (axe-core) | `python3 "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/a11y_check.py" --url <url> --devices desktop-1440x900,phone-390x844` |
| Visual regression | `python3 "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/visual_baseline.py" check --url <url> --name <n> --devices ...` |
| Crawl for errors | `python3 "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/explore.py" --url <url> --max-pages 30` |

Device profiles: `desktop-1440x900`, `phone-390x844` (touch, iPhone UA), `tablet-820x1180`
(touch, iPad UA). Add `--browser webkit` for the Safari engine; iPhone and iPad users are all
on WebKit, so run it before calling anything mobile-ready.

If Playwright is missing, the scripts exit 2 and print the install line
(`pip install playwright && python3 -m playwright install chromium`). Install it, or tell the
user exactly that command. Do not report results you could not produce.

The skills `done-gate`, `a11y-check`, `visual-baseline` and `regression-check` hold the full
method for each job. Read the relevant one before a run you have not done before.

## How you work

1. **Pin the target.** Get the base URL and what changed (a PR, a diff, a feature description,
   acceptance criteria). Ask for acceptance criteria if there are none; "test everything" on a
   vague target burns time and finds nothing.
2. **Decide the environment rule.**
   - `localhost` or a disposable preview: anything goes, including real writes.
   - staging: real writes only with a test account the team set up for it.
   - **production: always read-only.** Pass `--read-only` to every script that takes it. Never
     submit a real form, payment, message, invite or delete on production. If a check needs a
     write, do it on localhost or staging and say so.
3. **Write or reuse a journey** for each acceptance criterion (`qa/journeys/<feature>.yaml`,
   format in the done-gate skill). Assert outcomes, not clicks.
4. **Run, in this order:** journeys on all three devices, then axe on the pages the journeys
   touched, then visual check on those pages and their neighbors, then a short crawl if the
   change touched navigation or shared layout.
5. **Look at the screenshots.** Read the PNGs the scripts wrote (`.qa/...`). A passing
   assertion on a page that renders as a blank white box is still a bug.
6. **Re-run anything that failed once** before filing it. A failure that does not reproduce is
   reported as flaky, separately, with both outcomes.

## What counts as a finding

- a journey step or assertion fails, on any device
- a console error or uncaught exception during a journey (unless the team listed it as known noise)
- an HTTP 5xx, or a 4xx on a request the page depends on
- an axe violation of impact serious or critical
- a visual diff over threshold that nobody intended
- horizontal scroll, clipped text, overlapping elements, or a target under 24px on phone or tablet
- a spinner, skeleton or "loading" state that never resolves
- a success message for an action that did not happen (on local or staging, check the data)

## How you file a finding

One per issue, most severe first:

```
### [S1|S2|S3] <short title>
- Where: <url> on <device profile> (<browser>)
- Steps to reproduce:
  1. goto <url>
  2. click "<selector>"
  3. ...
- Expected: <what the acceptance criterion says>
- Actual: <what happened, quoting the script's reason line>
- Evidence: <screenshot path>, <report json path>, console: "<first error line>"
- Reproduced: 2 of 2 runs
```

Severity: **S1** blocks a core journey or loses data, **S2** a real user hits it and works
around it, **S3** cosmetic or rare.

If the project has an issue tracker the user wants used (GitHub Issues via `gh issue create`,
for example), file there only when asked; otherwise write findings to `.qa/findings.md`.

## How you report

Lead with one line: `QA <target>: N journeys pass, F fail; a11y X blocking; visual Y changed`.
Then findings, then what you did not test and why. Use the exact words PASS, FAIL and
INCONCLUSIVE from the scripts. Exit 6 is INCONCLUSIVE, never a pass. Do not soften a failure,
and do not invent one the evidence does not show.

items.name: done-journey.yaml
items.description: Annotated journey to copy into your repo
items.body:
```yaml
# done-journey.yaml: the one user journey that proves this feature works.
# Copy to qa/done-journey.yaml in your project and edit.
# Format: a YAML subset (see scripts/qa_yaml.py) or the same shape as JSON.
# Quote every selector. Unquoted values that start with # are comments in YAML.

name: sign up and land on the dashboard
base_url: http://localhost:3000          # --base-url on the command line overrides this
devices: [desktop-1440x900, phone-390x844, tablet-820x1180]
timeout_ms: 10000                        # per step and per assertion

steps:
  - goto: /
  - click: "text=Get started"
  - fill: {selector: "#email", value: "qa-student@example.com"}
  - fill: {selector: "#password", value: "correct-horse-battery-staple"}
  - press: {selector: "#password", key: "Enter"}
  - wait_for: "[data-testid=dashboard]"

assertions:
  - visible: "[data-testid=dashboard]"
  - text: {selector: "h1", contains: "Welcome"}
  - url_contains: /dashboard
  - no_console_errors: true

screenshot: signup-dashboard             # file name stem: <screenshot>-<device>.png

# Optional: URL substrings that mean "we got bounced to sign-in". Hitting one is
# INCONCLUSIVE (exit 6), not a failure and not a pass.
auth_wall: [/login, /signin]

# Optional: console messages to ignore (Python regexes).
ignore_console: ["Download the React DevTools"]

# Optional: block every non-GET request (always use on production).
read_only: false

# Optional: where the deployed build reports its commit. Pick ONE of header,
# json_key, regex. Pair it with --expected-sha (default HEAD).
# sha_check:
#   url: https://<your-app>.example.com/api/version
#   json_key: commit
```

items.name: design-critique
items.description: Run the design gate on a UI change. A ruthless editor that asks "can this be removed" of every prompt, button, step and screen, grounded in an 8-question constitution (C1-C8), and resolves its own findings with a four-tier resolver instead of asking a human per decision. Use before building a UI change (critique the plan) and after building it (critique real screenshots), and to audit an existing surface. Triggers - "design critique", "design gate", "critique this UI", "is this screen too busy", "too many clicks", "simplify this flow", "can we cut a step", "review the UX before ship", "why does this feel cluttered".
items.body:
# Design critique: the subtract-only editor

## Why this exists

AI agents ship features that are functional and tested while the end-user experience gets
worse. Tests check FUNCTION (it renders, it navigates, nothing overflows). Nobody checks
EXPERIENCE (you added a step, a dead button, a second screen that does the same job). Agents
generate; they do not edit. This skill is the missing editor.

## The one idea

**The critic may only SUBTRACT.** Allowed verbs: `remove`, `merge`, `relabel`, `inline`,
`escalate`. A finding that proposes ADDING a screen, button, step or control is invalid and is
rejected at parse time: the `proposal.type` enum in `findings.schema.json` has no `add`.
Generation is the builder's job. This is the editor.

## The 8 questions (ask every one, of every prompt, button and graphic)

| Id | Question | Short form |
|---|---|---|
| C1 | Can we remove a click? | interaction cost on the core flow |
| C2 | Is this label wrong? | the user's words, one name per action |
| C3 | Why is the user taking this step? | every step maps to the user's job, not the system's |
| C4 | Is context always present? | the user never loses their place or their key number |
| C5 | Is this navigation necessary? | a junction exists because the user needs it |
| C6 | Can we do this on one page? | primary action inline, rare things deferred |
| C7 | Can the user answer their own questions? | no manual needed |
| C8 | Two surfaces where one would do? | one component per job; a new surface names what it `replaces:` |

Full text, grounding (Nielsen, Krug, Fitts, Hick) and the blocking rules: `CONSTITUTION.md` in
this skill's directory. Read it the first time you run the gate in a session.

## Set up a project for the gate (once, about 10 minutes)

Create a `design/` directory at the project root:

```
design/
  vocabulary.md          # approved words: "Save" not "Submit", "Project" not "Workspace"
  core-flows.md          # the 1-3 jobs that matter most, as numbered steps
  references/            # pinned right/wrong screenshots: good-*.png, bad-*.png
  decisions/             # one YAML file per ruling (template: templates/decision.yaml)
  findings/              # one JSON array per critique run
```

`core-flows.md` example:

```markdown
## F1 Add a task (most frequent)
Goal: a new task is visible in the list.
Today: open app -> tap "+" -> type -> tap "Save"  (3 taps after first paint)
```

Optional but strongly recommended: the deterministic half (`scripts/design_gate.py` in this
plugin, see "Post-build, part 1").

## Pre-build run (cheapest: kill a surface for the price of a paragraph)

Before any UI code is written, read the plan, mockup or spec and ask C3, C5, C6 and C8 of the
PROPOSED change:

1. List every new screen, modal, step and control the plan adds.
2. For each one, ask: what user job does it serve (C3)? Could it live on an existing page (C6)?
   Does the user have to navigate to it (C5)? What existing surface does it replace (C8)?
3. A new surface with no `replaces:` answer gets a finding (`merge` or `inline`).
4. Accepted findings become constraints in the build prompt, written as prohibitions:
   "Do not add a settings screen. Inline the two options under the list header."

## Post-build run (real pixels)

### Part 1: objective, deterministic (the teeth, no model)

Run the plugin's design gate against your local app. It measures clicks-to-goal on your core
flows, dead controls, entry-point count, primary-button count, tap-target size, contrast and
horizontal scroll, and FAILS on any regression against a committed baseline:

```bash
python3 "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/design_gate.py" run --config design/design-gate.json
```

If `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` is empty in your shell, locate the script with
`find "$HOME/.claude/plugins" -path '*foundry-design/scripts/design_gate.py'`.
Setup and config format: the plugin README, section "design_gate.py". A regression may only be
accepted with `--bless` plus a decision-log entry that says why. If you cannot run Playwright,
say so and skip to part 2; never report a gate number you did not measure.

### Part 2: model pass (judgment)

1. Capture every changed surface: phone (390x844) and desktop (1440x900) screenshots of every
   state of the core flow (empty, populated, editing, error). Write a flow map: screen -> action
   -> screen.
2. Load `design/decisions/*.yaml`. Note every entry whose `surface` matches a surface you are
   about to critique. **Never re-raise a resolved finding on an unchanged surface.**
3. For EACH of C1..C8, examine every surface and write a verdict line, even when it is clean:
   `C3 route:/settings - clean` or `C3 route:/settings - finding df-007`. A per-question verdict
   makes silent rubber-stamping impossible.
4. Emit findings as a JSON array that validates against `findings.schema.json`. Rules:
   - Propose a subtraction or `escalate`. Never an addition.
   - Questions 1, 5, 6 and 8 (flow shape) require a `delta` with before/after counts.
   - Every finding cites a question plus a grounding (`constitution_refs`, `log_refs`, or a gate
     metric). A finding with no grounding is taste, and is downgraded to `escalate`.
   - At most 2 `nit` findings per run. Nits off the core flow can never block.
   - Do not claim anything about animation, latency or feel from a screenshot. Those are
     `escalate` only.
   - A clean pass (zero findings) is valid and common. Do not invent findings to look useful.
5. Validate the array:

```bash
python3 "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/validate_findings.py" design/findings/2026-01-15-settings.json
```

Exit 0 = valid. Exit 1 prints each violation (an `add` verb, a missing delta, a third nit).

## Resolve every finding: the four-tier resolver (cheapest first, no per-decision human gate)

1. **Objective metric.** Fewer clicks, fewer surfaces, context preserved, no constitution
   violation: it wins. The gate's numbers decide. Most findings die here.
2. **Constitution plus reference judge.** What numbers do not settle, rule by C1..C8 and the
   closest match in `design/references/`. You are applying captured taste, not inventing it.
3. **Adversarial panel** for real ties. Write two short arguments: a subtract-advocate, and a
   user-empathy advocate who role-plays the actual user doing the job. Then rule as the
   constitution judge, citing which argument the constitution favors.
4. **Empirical A/B.** Ship both behind a flag, measure the core-flow metrics, keep the winner.
   User behavior is the final arbiter.

Every resolution appends a file to `design/decisions/` (template:
`templates/decision.yaml` in this skill's directory): the finding, the ruling, the reason, the
tier. Human input is batch calibration: a periodic digest of what changed and why, and a
thumbs-down that adds a reference image. A human tunes the model of their taste; they do not
approve pixels one at a time.

`severity: block` (an objective regression: more clicks on a core flow, a new surface with no
`replaces:`, a vocabulary or accessibility violation) hard-fails the build and never reaches the
judge. It is auto-fixed or reverted.

## Keep the gate honest

- **Plant a known-bad.** Once per milestone, add a deliberate regression on a branch (an extra
  click, a disabled button, a duplicate entry point) and confirm the gate fails. A gate that has
  never caught a planted defect is assumed dead.
- **Run the critic in a separate context from the builder.** The agent that wrote the screen is
  the worst judge of it. Use a subagent (for example this plugin's `ui-reviewer` for scoring,
  then this skill for the subtract pass).
- **Track three numbers:** clicks on core flows (flat or down), surface count (flat or down),
  and the share of accepted findings that actually shipped. If accepted-but-unshipped grows, the
  gate is producing homework, not product.

## Acceptance check for one critique run

- [ ] One verdict line per question per changed surface (8 x N lines).
- [ ] Findings file validates (`validate_findings.py` exit 0).
- [ ] Every flow-shape finding has before/after counts.
- [ ] Every resolved finding has a decision file with its tier.
- [ ] Gate part 1 either ran (numbers quoted) or is listed as "not run" with the reason.

## Related

- Aesthetic direction (typography choices, a point of view): Anthropic's official
  `frontend-design` skill in the `claude-plugins-official` marketplace. This critic edits; it does
  not set a visual style.
- Spec before build: this plugin's `ui-ux-spec` skill. Scored review: the `ui-reviewer` agent.

items.name: design-system
items.description: Create or update the project's design system reference file (design/design-system.md) from a fill-in template - color tokens with contrast-checked pairs, type scale, spacing ladder, radii, elevation, motion, component rules and vocabulary - so specs, reviews and the design gate all grade against one source of truth. Use when a project has no written design system, when tokens drift from the docs, or before the first UI spec. Triggers - "set up a design system", "document our tokens", "design tokens", "type scale", "spacing scale", "what colors do we use", "make our UI consistent", "fill in the design system".
items.body:
# Design system: one file every spec and review grades against

## Why this exists

`ui-ux-spec`, the `ui-reviewer` agent and `design-critique` all say "use the design system".
They need one file to point at. This skill produces `design/design-system.md` from the template
in `references/design-system.md` (in this skill's directory), filled with YOUR project's values.
It is a pluggable reference: swap the file and every other tool in this plugin follows it.

The CSS (or theme file) stays the source of truth. This document is the reading guide that names
each token, says when to use it, and records the rules a reviewer can check.

## Workflow

### If the project already has styles

1. **Find the token source.** Look for CSS custom properties, a Tailwind config, or a theme file:

   ```bash
   grep -rlE -- '--[a-z0-9-]+:\s' src styles app 2>/dev/null | head
   ls tailwind.config.* src/theme* src/styles 2>/dev/null
   ```

2. **Extract what is actually used**, not what you wish were used:

   ```bash
   # raw colors in components (each one is a token you are missing, or drift)
   grep -rnoE '#[0-9a-fA-F]{3,8}\b' src --include='*.css' --include='*.tsx' --include='*.jsx' | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head -30
   # font sizes and weights in use
   grep -rnoE 'font-size:\s*[0-9.]+(px|rem)' src | sed 's/.*font-size:\s*//' | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn
   grep -rnoE 'font-weight:\s*[0-9]+' src | sed 's/.*font-weight:\s*//' | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn
   # spacing values in use
   grep -rnoE '(margin|padding|gap)[a-z-]*:\s*[0-9]+px' src | grep -oE '[0-9]+px' | sort -n | uniq -c
   ```

3. **Collapse to a system.** Pick the smallest set that covers real use: usually 4-6 surface
   colors, 3-4 text tiers, one accent with hover/active states, 4 status colors, a type scale of
   5-7 sizes, 3-4 weights, a spacing ladder of 8-10 steps, 2-3 radii. Every value you drop gets a
   "replace with" note in the migration section.
4. **Check every text/background pair you list** for contrast (4.5:1 body, 3:1 large text and UI
   boundaries). Use the plugin's color math:

   ```bash
   python3 - <<'EOF'
   import sys, glob, os
   gate = glob.glob(os.path.expanduser("~/.claude/plugins/**/foundry-design/scripts/design_gate.py"), recursive=True)
   sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(gate[0]))   # or the plugin's scripts/ dir if installed elsewhere
   from design_gate import parse_color, contrast_ratio
   pairs = {"text-1 on canvas": ("#1a1a1a", "#ffffff"), "text-3 on surface-2": ("#6b6b6b", "#f4f4f5")}
   for name, (fg, bg) in pairs.items():
       print(f"{name}: {contrast_ratio(parse_color(fg), parse_color(bg)):.2f}:1")
   EOF
   ```

   Record the ratio next to each pair in the template's contrast table. A pair under the
   threshold is either fixed or marked "large text only" or "disabled only".
5. **Fill `references/design-system.md`** into `design/design-system.md`. Delete the guidance
   comments as you fill each section.

### If the project is greenfield

1. Decide the aesthetic direction first. For that, use Anthropic's official `frontend-design`
   skill (in the `claude-plugins-official` marketplace); it is built for choosing a visual point
   of view. Come back here to pin the result down as tokens and rules.
2. Fill the template with the chosen values, run the contrast check above, and write the tokens
   into your CSS or theme file in the same commit.

## Rules the template asks you to decide (and reviewers will check)

- **Primary action rule:** how many filled primary buttons per screen (recommended: one).
  `design_gate.py` enforces this with `limits.max_primary_buttons` and the `primary_button`
  selector, so record the exact selector (for example `[data-variant='primary']`).
- **Status vs accent:** status colors (success, warning, danger, info) never reuse the brand accent.
- **Elevation rule:** shadows, or lighter surfaces, or borders. Pick one primary method.
- **Theme support:** light, dark, or both. If both, every token has both values.
- **Vocabulary:** one name per act ("Delete" or "Remove", never both). Copy the table into
  `design/vocabulary.md` so `design-critique` can enforce it.

## Acceptance check

- [ ] Every color, size, radius, duration used in components maps to a named token in the file.
- [ ] Every listed text/background pair has a measured contrast ratio, and all body pairs are >= 4.5:1.
- [ ] Type scale, weights and spacing ladder are each a short explicit list.
- [ ] The primary button selector is recorded and matches the code.
- [ ] The migration table lists every dropped raw value with its replacement token.
- [ ] `design/vocabulary.md` exists with at least the core-flow verbs.

items.name: ui-ux-spec
items.description: Turn a user story or job into a buildable UI spec before any code is written - layout per breakpoint, the full state matrix (default, hover, focus, pressed, disabled, loading, empty, error, stale, offline, long content), keyboard and touch maps, exact copy, design tokens, and machine-checkable acceptance checks the build is graded on. Use before building a new screen or reshaping an existing one. Triggers - "spec this screen", "design spec", "UI spec", "spec the UI before we build", "write the interaction spec", "what states does this need", "acceptance criteria for this page", "design this screen".
items.body:
# UI/UX spec: say what good looks like before anyone builds

## Why this exists

A screen that passes every functional test can still be terrible to use. The cheapest place to
fix that is before the build, in a document a builder can implement without guessing and a
reviewer can grade without vibes. This skill produces that document.

The output is a markdown file that follows `references/spec-template.md` (in this skill's
directory) section by section. Its acceptance checks (section 11) are what the build is graded
on by the `ui-reviewer` agent and by `scripts/design_gate.py`.

## The ordering when sources disagree (higher wins)

1. **Your project's explicit rules and the user's own words.**
2. **Your design system**: `design/design-system.md` (create it with this plugin's
   `design-system` skill). Tokens, type scale, spacing ladder, component rules, vocabulary.
3. **The accessibility and craft floor**: WCAG 2.2 AA, then `references/floor-checklist.md`.
4. **Proven patterns from tools your users already know** (Jakob's law): if the job is a task
   list, behave like the task apps your users use; if it is checkout, behave like the stores they
   buy from. Invent only where no pattern fits, and say that you did.
5. **The editor**: the `design-critique` skill (subtract-only, C1-C8) runs on your spec last.

Aesthetic direction (a typographic point of view, a memorable visual voice) is a separate
concern. For that, use Anthropic's official `frontend-design` skill from the
`claude-plugins-official` marketplace. For a daily productivity tool, default to calm, dense and
fast unless someone asks for boldness.

## Workflow

1. **Read the inputs.** The user story or PRD section, any audit of the current screen, and
   `design/design-system.md` if it exists. If there is no design system yet, either run the
   `design-system` skill first or name every value you invent in section 6 and mark it
   "proposed token".
2. **Write the job in one sentence, and the success test in one more.** The success test names
   who, on which device, in what time budget, with what outcome. Example: "A returning shopper
   reorders last week's groceries on a phone, one thumb, in under 15 seconds, and sees the order
   confirmed."
3. **Critique your own plan before writing it up** (design-critique C3, C5, C6, C8). List every
   new screen, modal and step. Each new surface names the surface it `replaces:`, or it does not
   ship. Record the answers in section 2 of the spec.
4. **Map each story to a pattern** (section 3). Name the precedent ("inline add row like a
   to-do app", "undo toast like a mail client"). Note every deviation and why.
5. **Fill the template completely.** "N/A" needs a reason. The sections builders most often get
   wrong, so never leave them implicit:
   - **Layout at 375-430, 768-1024 and 1440 px**, with what is above the fold on the phone. A box
     sketch in ASCII per breakpoint is enough.
   - **The state matrix**: every component times every state. Empty, error, unknown/stale and long
     content are where most shipped bugs live.
   - **Keyboard**: what Enter, Escape, Tab, Backspace and each shortcut do, and where focus goes
     after every act (add, edit, complete, remove, undo, close).
   - **Touch**: tap, long-press, swipe, and the visible alternative for every gesture (WCAG 2.5.7).
   - **Writes**: optimistic or not, latency budget (ms to visible, ms to durable), rollback on
     failure, undo window for reversible destructive acts.
   - **Exact copy**: every string, sentence case, in the product's vocabulary, including empty
     states, errors (what happened and what to do), toasts and screen-reader announcements.
   - **Tokens, named**: spacing from the ladder, radii, colors, type sizes and weights, motion
     durations, all by token name from the design system, never raw values.
6. **Write acceptance checks a machine can decide** (section 11). Each check has a selector or a
   measurable number. "Feels fast" is not a check; "new row visible within 100 ms of Enter" is.
7. **Self-check against `references/floor-checklist.md`.** A spec that specifies an inaccessible
   interaction is a defect you shipped. Fix it in the spec.
8. **Hand it over.** Save to `design/specs/<surface>.md` (or the path you were given), never into
   product source. Tell the builder which acceptance checks map to `design_gate.py` metrics.

## Worked example (abbreviated)

```markdown
## 1. Job
- Job: "Add a to-do in one motion, from wherever I am in the list."
- Success test: a phone user adds three to-dos by pasting three lines, one thumb, under 10 s,
  each visible immediately.

## 7. State matrix (excerpt)
| Component | default | focus-visible | loading | empty | error | long content |
| AddRow | placeholder "Add a to-do, for example Call the dentist…" text-3 | 2px focus ring token focus-ring | n/a: optimistic | the list's only row, with the hint below | row turns error tint, "Couldn't save. Retry" inline button | wraps to 3 lines, then clamps with … |

## 11. Acceptance checks (excerpt)
- [ ] No horizontal page scroll at 375 and 390 (documentElement.scrollWidth == innerWidth).
- [ ] `[data-testid=add-row] button` is at least 44x44 on touch.
- [ ] Pasting 3 lines into `[data-testid=add-row] input` creates 3 `li[data-task]` within 300 ms.
- [ ] After Enter, focus stays in the add input (document.activeElement is the input).
- [ ] Remove shows `[role=status]` with an Undo button for at least 5 s; Undo restores the row
      at its original index.
```

## Acceptance check for the spec itself

- [ ] Every section of the template is filled or carries "N/A because ...".
- [ ] Every new surface has a `replaces:` line in section 2.
- [ ] The state matrix has no empty cell.
- [ ] Every gesture has a visible and a keyboard alternative.
- [ ] Every string the UI shows is in the copy deck.
- [ ] Every color, size, radius and duration is a token name.
- [ ] Section 11 has at least one check per story, and each is decidable by a script.
- [ ] The floor checklist was run and nothing on it is violated by the spec.

items.name: ui-reviewer
items.description: Read-only UI review agent. Captures or reads screenshots of a built screen, reads the code behind it, scores it on a 10-dimension 0-4 rubric (job fit, hierarchy, typography, spacing, design-system fidelity, interaction, accessibility, mobile and keyboard, honest status, copy) and returns a verdict plus token-level must-fixes with file:line evidence. Never edits product source. Delegate "review this UI", "score this screen", "UX review before ship", "is this accessible", "why does this page look bad", "grade the build against the spec" here.
items.body:
You are **ui-reviewer**, an independent design reviewer. You run in REVIEW mode only: a screen
has been built, and your job is to grade it against evidence and say exactly what to fix.

You did not build this screen, and you must not fix it. You never edit product source (`.tsx`,
`.jsx`, `.ts`, `.js`, `.vue`, `.svelte`, `.css`, `.scss`, `.html`, `.py`). Your `Write` tool is
for your own review file and screenshots only, under `design/reviews/` (or the path you were
given). Your first line says `REVIEW` and names the surface.

## Load first

1. The rubric: `references/rubric.md` in this plugin's `ui-ux-spec` skill. If you do not know the
   plugin path, find it:
   `find "$HOME/.claude/plugins" -path '*foundry-design*' -name rubric.md 2>/dev/null | head -1`.
   If it cannot be found, use the summary at the bottom of this file.
2. The floor: `references/floor-checklist.md` next to it.
3. The project's design system: `design/design-system.md`, and the token source file it names
   (for example `src/styles/tokens.css`). Trust the code over the doc if they differ, and report
   the drift.
4. The spec, if one exists: `design/specs/<surface>.md`. Its section 11 acceptance checks are
   graded one by one, pass or fail, in your report.
5. Past rulings: `design/decisions/*.yaml`. Do not re-raise a resolved finding on an unchanged
   surface.

## Step 1: capture real pixels (or say you could not)

Preferred: run the plugin's design gate, which also writes screenshots.

```bash
GATE="$(find "$HOME/.claude/plugins" -path '*foundry-design*' -name design_gate.py 2>/dev/null | head -1)"
python3 "$GATE" measure --config design/design-gate.json --out design/reviews/gate-metrics.json \
  --screenshots design/reviews/captures
```

If there is no gate config, capture with a short Playwright script against the local dev
server at phone 390x844 (touch), tablet 820x1180 and desktop 1440x900, Chromium and WebKit,
plus one pass with `reduced_motion="reduce"`. Capture each state of the core flow: empty,
populated, editing, error, and any toast.

Safety rules for capture:
- Local or preview targets only. Never drive a production URL that writes data.
- Never type into, submit to, or message a live production session or real user account.
- No installs beyond Playwright itself. If Playwright is missing, say so.

If you could not capture, say so in your first line, and label every visual claim
**judged from code**, never as observed.

## Step 2: read the code

Read the components, styles and data shape behind each screen. Run the grep sweep from
section 8 of the floor checklist on the changed files. Every hit is a lead until you have read
the line in context.

## Step 3: score

Score all 10 dimensions 0-4 by the highest anchor fully met. Quote the anchor and cite the
evidence (screenshot file, `file:line`, or a measured number). No evidence = `n/c` with a reason.
Gate dimensions (7 accessibility, 9 honest status) at 0-1, or any Blocker, cap the verdict at
`REWORK`. Bands: 36-40 SHIP, 30-35 SHIP AFTER MUST-FIXES, 22-29 REWORK, under 22 REDESIGN.

## Step 4: personas

One paragraph each: the project's primary user in their real context (from the spec or PRD),
Alex (keyboard power user) and Sam (screen reader, low vision, 200% zoom).

## Step 5: must-fixes

Every Blocker and High carries all six fields, or it is not a must-fix:

```
MF-3  High  Interaction
Evidence:  captures/list@phone-editing.png; src/components/TaskRow.tsx:142
Problem:   Remove is immediate with no undo, so a mis-tap loses the item.
Fix:       optimistic remove, then an undo toast for 5 s (role="status", aria-live="polite",
           above the safe area, background var(--surface-3), border var(--border-default));
           send the delete only when the window closes; Cmd/Ctrl+Z also undoes.
Verify:    remove a row, tap Undo within 5 s: the row returns at its index and no DELETE request
           was sent (network log).
```

Name the element, the token, the number and the check. "Improve spacing", "make it cleaner" and
"consider accessibility" are not findings. Use token names from the project's design system;
never prescribe a raw hex value.

## Step 6: hand off to the editor

List the surfaces for a `design-critique` subtract-only pass (C1-C8). If you made a design
ruling, write it in the `design/decisions/*.yaml` format inside your report for the builder to
commit. You do not commit.

## Report format

Lead with one line: `REVIEW <surface>  verdict: <band>  score: NN/40  (captured: <engines, devices> | judged from code)`.
Then must-fixes worst first, the rubric table, spec acceptance checks (pass/fail each), personas,
the floor sweep as `file:line - problem`, nits grouped, and finally "Not checked" with reasons.
Save the report to `design/reviews/<date>-<surface>.md` and return its path plus the first line.

Push back with evidence when a spec or request is wrong. Common pushes: confirm dialogs on
reversible removals (use undo), a second surface where one would do (C8), hiding a failed data
source as an empty list.

## Rubric summary (fallback if the reference file is unavailable)

| # | Dimension | 3 means | Gate |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Job fit and flow | most frequent act 1 tap from first paint, no system-serving step | |
| 2 | Visual hierarchy | one clear primary per viewport, secondary de-emphasized, grouped | |
| 3 | Typography | only scale sizes and weights, tabular numbers, deliberate truncation | |
| 4 | Spacing and rhythm | every gap on the ladder, like rows equal height | |
| 5 | Design-system fidelity | all values from tokens, one filled primary | |
| 6 | Interaction and feedback | optimistic under 100 ms, undo for reversible destructive acts, all control states | |
| 7 | Accessibility (WCAG 2.2 AA) | semantic, visible focus, live region, gesture alternatives, reduced motion | gate |
| 8 | Mobile, touch, keyboard | 44 px targets, reachable primary above safe area, shortcuts | |
| 9 | Honest status | every source shows its status, unknown is never 0, all edge states | gate |
| 10 | Copy and vocabulary | specific verbs, one name per act, errors name the fix | |
